arkaroola-mars-oz.access_and_facilities: Most visitors arrive by car, and flights can be chartered from Adelaide. The sanctuary has a village and a network of four-wheel-drive tracks.
arkaroola-mars-oz.climate: The area has a subtropical desert climate under the Koppen system.

facts.label: Algal mat survives spring water temperature

arkaroola-mars-oz.hazards: Radon gas collects near the Paralana springs and prolonged stays there may be a health hazard.

arkaroola-mars-oz.place: Arkaroola Wilderness Sanctuary, northern Flinders Ranges, South Australia, Australia
arkaroola-mars-oz.summary: Arkaroola is a wildlife sanctuary in the northern Flinders Ranges that Mars Society Australia selected as a Mars analog region. Its site report says the case rested on a mix of logistical convenience and scientific value, including a fossil hydrothermal system around Mount Painter and the Paralana hot springs. A research station called Mars-Oz was proposed for the gravel plains east of the zone.
arkaroola-mars-oz.terrain_geology: The area has rugged ranges, a fossil hydrothermal system with an alteration halo, and the Paralana hot springs, which are radioactive and heated without a magma source.

askja-caldera.access_and_facilities: The central volcano region can only be reached for a few months of the year.
askja-caldera.climate: Askja lies in the rain shadow north-east of the Vatnajökull glacier, so rainfall is low for Iceland.
askja-caldera.hazards: It is an active volcano with a long record of eruptions, and the area is cut off by snow for much of the year.

image.author: Michael Ryan
image.credit: Photo: Michael Ryan, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Caldera of Askja volcano

askja-caldera.place: Askja caldera, Dyngjufjöll mountains, central highlands, Iceland
askja-caldera.summary: Askja is an active volcano in a remote part of the central highlands of Iceland. It is a complex of nested calderas inside the Dyngjufjöll mountains. NASA used the area to train Apollo astronauts in geology before the lunar missions.
askja-caldera.terrain_geology: The central volcano holds several nested calderas, including the main summit caldera, a smaller caldera to its north-east, and the lake-filled caldera formed in the late nineteenth century. Most eruptions from the system are small, basaltic and effusive.

atacama-desert-cmu-nomad-rover-traverse.access_and_facilities: Coastal towns such as Antofagasta and the inland town of Calama serve the region, and most visitors to the interior stay in San Pedro de Atacama. Nomad is now on display at the Atacama Desert Museum in Antofagasta.
atacama-desert-cmu-nomad-rover-traverse.climate: It is hyperarid, with some weather stations never recording rain. Temperatures stay mild through most of the year, with only a few freezing periods in winter.
atacama-desert-cmu-nomad-rover-traverse.hazards: Extreme aridity and long distances from supply towns make field work demanding.

image.author: L. Honnorat/ESO
image.credit: Photo: L. Honnorat/ESO, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Atacama Desert Landscape (iced moment 870-CC)

atacama-desert-cmu-nomad-rover-traverse.place: Atacama Desert, northern Chile (area of the Nomad rover trek)
atacama-desert-cmu-nomad-rover-traverse.summary: The Atacama Desert is a desert plateau on the Pacific coast of northern Chile and is the driest nonpolar desert in the world. Carnegie Mellon University drove its Nomad rover across it, remotely from the United States, as a field test of technology for planetary exploration. The desert is also used for Mars expedition simulations because of its similarities to the Martian environment.
atacama-desert-cmu-nomad-rover-traverse.terrain_geology: The desert is a low-relief bench between the Andes and the Chilean Coast Range, with salt flats such as the Salar de Atacama and basins that have no outflow to the sea. Soft sand was one of the surfaces Nomad had to cross.

atacama-desert-yungay-core.access_and_facilities: The University of Antofagasta Desert Research Station is located near the Yungay area in the Antofagasta Region.
atacama-desert-yungay-core.climate: Rain is almost absent. Some places have gone years without any, and some weather stations have never recorded rain. A marine fog called camanchaca supplies moisture to some locations.
atacama-desert-yungay-core.hazards: Rare heavy rain has triggered deadly mudflows in the region.

image.author: Diego Delso
image.credit: Photo: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Valle de la Luna, San Pedro de Atacama, Atacama Desert (not the Yungay site itself)

atacama-desert-yungay-core.place: Yungay area, Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region, Chile
atacama-desert-yungay-core.summary: The Atacama is a plateau desert on the Pacific coast of northern Chile, and the area around the abandoned Yungay mining town is commonly called the driest place in the world. The desert has been used for Mars expedition simulations, and NASA uses it to test instruments for future Mars missions. In a published test, researchers repeated the Viking life-detection experiments on Yungay-region soil and found no signs of life.
atacama-desert-yungay-core.terrain_geology: Soils in parts of the Atacama have been compared to Martian soil. Perchlorates, which were also found on Mars by the Phoenix lander, occur in the desert along with nitrate deposits that contain organics.

atacama-maria-elena-south.climate: A cold desert climate with mild temperatures through the year. Some weather stations in the desert have never recorded rain.

facts.label: Desert length along the Pacific coast
Year Maria Elena South was reported

atacama-maria-elena-south.hazards: Rare rain can cause flash floods and mudflows, and some areas support no plant or animal life at all.

atacama-maria-elena-south.place: Maria Elena South, Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region, Chile
atacama-maria-elena-south.summary: Maria Elena South is a hyperarid site in the Atacama Desert, near the former nitrate mining town of Maria Elena. Researchers reported it as much drier than the better-known Yungay site and as a better Mars-like environment. Soil in the wider Atacama has been compared with Martian soil, and NASA uses the desert to test instruments for future Mars missions.
atacama-maria-elena-south.terrain_geology: The desert is a low-relief bench, like a giant uplifted terrace, with evaporite formations and large deposits of nitrate, iodine-bearing minerals, copper and lithium.

axel-heiberg-gypsum-hill-and-lost-hammer.access_and_facilities: The island has no permanent residents. The McGill Arctic Research Station sits inland from Expedition Fiord and operates from March to August.
axel-heiberg-gypsum-hill-and-lost-hammer.climate: Polar, with continuous permafrost and winter darkness from roughly October to February.

axel-heiberg-gypsum-hill-and-lost-hammer.place: Gypsum Hill and Lost Hammer springs, Axel Heiberg Island, Nunavut, Canada
axel-heiberg-gypsum-hill-and-lost-hammer.summary: Axel Heiberg Island is an uninhabited island in the Canadian High Arctic. Lost Hammer is a cold, very salty, oxygen-poor spring that flows up through thick permafrost. Researchers study it as an analog for possible Martian subsurface brines and methane, and the McGill Arctic Research Station on the island has been used for Mars analog work. The sources read describe Lost Hammer in detail but say little about Gypsum Hill.
axel-heiberg-gypsum-hill-and-lost-hammer.terrain_geology: The spring emerges through a gypsum and anhydrite diapir and builds a hollow salt tufa cone that empties and refills with the seasons.

barranco-del-jaroso-sierra-almagrera.access_and_facilities: The range lies near the Mediterranean coast within the municipality of Cuevas del Almanzora. It is part of an EU protected area for its flora and fauna.

facts.label: Year mining of the range resumed

barranco-del-jaroso-sierra-almagrera.place: Barranco del Jaroso (Jaroso ravine), Sierra Almagrera, Almeria province, Spain
barranco-del-jaroso-sierra-almagrera.summary: The Jaroso ravine is the type locality of the mineral jarosite, first described there by August Breithaupt. Researchers have proposed its hydrothermal system as a model for Mars exploration because jarosite was later detected on Mars by the Opportunity rover. It has also been used to test Raman, laser-induced breakdown and Mossbauer instruments on Mars-relevant minerals.
barranco-del-jaroso-sierra-almagrera.terrain_geology: The range rose from the seabed along many faults that later filled with lead and silver ore veins. Alunite-group minerals, including jarosite and natrojarosite, dominate the ravine.

beacon-valley-and-university-valley-dry-.access_and_facilities: The valleys are inside a specially managed Antarctic area and are reached from the McMurdo Station region by research programmes.
beacon-valley-and-university-valley-dry-.climate: The Dry Valleys are a cold desert shaped by katabatic winds and a snow shadow behind the Transantarctic Mountains. At the higher sites, air temperatures stay below freezing.
beacon-valley-and-university-valley-dry-.hazards: Extreme cold and wind, and strict environmental protection rules apply.

image.author: Josh Landis, NSF
image.credit: Photo: Josh Landis, NSF, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Helicopter landing at Beacon Valley, Dry Valleys

beacon-valley-and-university-valley-dry-.place: Beacon Valley and University Valley, Quartermain Mountains, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Victoria Land, Antarctica
beacon-valley-and-university-valley-dry-.summary: Beacon Valley is an ice-free valley in the Quartermain Mountains of Victoria Land, part of the McMurdo Dry Valleys. University Valley is a small side valley that drains into it. Researchers describe the high-elevation Dry Valleys as one of the closest Earth matches for Martian ground ice, because dry permafrost sits over ice-cemented ground.
beacon-valley-and-university-valley-dry-.terrain_geology: The valley floors are mostly bare, loose gravel with ice-wedge polygons. Ice lies a short distance under the surface, as massive ground ice in middle Beacon Valley and as ice-cemented ground under dry permafrost in University Valley.

black-point-lava-flow.access_and_facilities: The site is close to Flagstaff, so crews and vehicles avoid the cost and travel time of reaching real planetary sites. Aerospace firms and university students are within reach.
black-point-lava-flow.climate: It is a high-elevation desert with hot summers. Test crews worked in summer heat during the simulated mission.

facts.label: Desert RATS Lunar Electric Rover tests year

black-point-lava-flow.hazards: Test slopes were steep, the ground is rough, and rovers can break down.

black-point-lava-flow.place: Black Point Lava Flow, near Flagstaff, northern Arizona, USA
black-point-lava-flow.summary: Black Point Lava Flow is a broad band of dark basalt in northern Arizona. It was first identified as a candidate lunar analog in the Apollo era, and NASA's Desert Research and Technology Studies group holds a technology test there every year, including Lunar Electric Rover trials and a simulated mission to the Malapert Massif region of the Moon. It is a testing ground for equipment, operations and human factors.
black-point-lava-flow.terrain_geology: Thick black basaltic lava pooled against the Little Colorado River and formed a ridge. The surrounding high desert has lava flows, volcanic cones and rough ground that resembles the Moon and Mars in shape.

bockfjord-volcanic-complex-amase.access_and_facilities: Field teams based themselves in Ny-Alesund or aboard a research vessel, with helicopter support.

facts.label: Mars meteorite with similar carbonate globules

bockfjord-volcanic-complex-amase.place: Bockfjord volcanic complex, Bockfjorden, Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway
bockfjord-volcanic-complex-amase.summary: The Bockfjord Volcanic Complex is a group of volcanic centres on the western side of Bockfjorden in northern Spitsbergen, including Sverrefjellet and Sigurdfjellet. The Arctic Mars Analog Svalbard Expedition (AMASE) works here to adapt instruments for Mars life-detection missions. Carbonate globules in the volcanic rocks resemble those in a well-studied Mars meteorite, and how they formed is still debated.
bockfjord-volcanic-complex-amase.terrain_geology: Rock types include basalt, peridotite xenoliths and clays, with hot-spring travertines and carbonate globules in basalt. The area also has warm springs, subsurface ice and sedimentary red beds.

bodele-depression-diatomite-deflation-ba.access_and_facilities: Faya-Largeau is the largest nearby town. We found no other access information.
bodele-depression-diatomite-deflation-ba.climate: Strong low-level winds are channelled between the two mountain ranges and raise dust, most often from October to March.
bodele-depression-diatomite-deflation-ba.hazards: Frequent dust storms, including a major event that reached West Africa and the Cape Verde Islands.

bodele-depression-diatomite-deflation-ba.summary: The Bodele Depression is a dry lake basin at the southern edge of the Sahara in northern Chad. Its floor is made of fine diatom sediment left by the former Mega-Lake Chad, and it is one of the strongest dust sources on Earth. The sources we read do not describe it as a Mars analog; GSOP lists it as a candidate not in our reference list because of its dust output.
bodele-depression-diatomite-deflation-ba.terrain_geology: A dry basin between the Tibesti and Ennedi mountains. Exposed lakebed sediment, including fossil diatoms, breaks down into fine dust.

bunge-land-zemlya-bunge.access_and_facilities: Uninhabited, with no facilities listed in the source read.
bunge-land-zemlya-bunge.hazards: Storm surges flood most of the surface.

image.author: NASA GIBS
image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Bunge Land (Zemlya Bunge), centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

bunge-land-zemlya-bunge.place: Bunge Land (Zemlya Bunge), New Siberian Islands, Sakha Republic, Russia
bunge-land-zemlya-bunge.summary: Bunge Land is a flat, sandy and almost bare plain between Kotelny and Faddeyevsky islands in the New Siberian Islands, off the northern coast of Siberia. Most of it floods during storm surges, and it has almost no vegetation or people. The page read does not describe any analog use, so its place on our list rests on GSOP's own screening as a candidate not in our reference list.
bunge-land-zemlya-bunge.terrain_geology: The surface is sandy and very flat, with a small slightly higher area in the southeast.

channeled-scablands-dry-falls.access_and_facilities: Dry Falls can be viewed from an interpretive center in Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park, on the state route near Coulee City. Parking needs a Discover Pass.

image.author: Steven Pavlov
image.credit: Photo: Steven Pavlov, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Dry Falls, Washington

channeled-scablands-dry-falls.place: Channeled Scablands and Dry Falls, central Washington, United States
channeled-scablands-dry-falls.summary: The Channeled Scablands are bare basalt channels and basins carved by repeated glacial outburst floods. Planetary scientists regard them as perhaps the best terrestrial analog of Martian outflow channels. Dry Falls is a dry cataract in the Scablands that is easy to visit and shows the scale of the flood erosion.
channeled-scablands-dry-falls.terrain_geology: Floods stripped the loess cover and exposed basalt, leaving a pattern of linked channels, coulees, cataracts and rock basins. Dry Falls is a scalloped cliff with four large alcoves and plunge pools at its base.

chott-el-djerid.access_and_facilities: The towns of Tozeur and Kebili sit on its edges. The lake can be crossed on foot or by car, and a road crossing exists, but the salt crust is not always firm.
chott-el-djerid.climate: The climate is hot desert, with very little rain and strong summer sunshine that evaporates the water.
chott-el-djerid.hazards: The salt crust can give way, which makes crossing off the roads dangerous.

image.author: Kais photographies

image.title: Chott el Djerid salt lake

chott-el-djerid.place: Chott el Djerid, between Tozeur and Kebili, central Tunisia
chott-el-djerid.summary: Chott el Djerid is a large salt lake in central Tunisia and the largest salt pan of the Sahara. It is flat and covered with salt crust, and it dries out almost completely in summer. In this project it is a candidate not in our reference list, and the sources checked here do not document planetary analog use.
chott-el-djerid.terrain_geology: The lake bottom is a flat evaporite basin that appears in shades of white, green and purple at different times.

cinder-lake-crater-field.access_and_facilities: The fields lie off the Forest Service road signed as the Cinder Hills off-road vehicle area, just south of the Sunset Crater turnoff from the main highway. Visiting on weekdays is suggested because the area is busy with off-road vehicles.
cinder-lake-crater-field.climate: Semi-arid, cool high plateau; snow in winter; monsoon storms in late summer.
cinder-lake-crater-field.hazards: Wind and off-road driving have badly worn the craters; the first field is farther from the main riding areas and is better preserved.

image.author: U.S. Geological Survey
image.credit: Photo: U.S. Geological Survey, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Cinder Lake Crater Field (creation of Crater Field 2)

cinder-lake-crater-field.place: Cinder Lake crater fields, near Sunset Crater, northeast of Flagstaff, Arizona, USA
cinder-lake-crater-field.summary: The Cinder Lake crater fields are artificial craters that the USGS Astrogeology branch blasted into cinder-covered ground in the Apollo era. They were built to match a Lunar Orbiter image of the Moon so astronauts could rehearse driving, navigation and sampling. Crews also tested lunar module and rover trainers there.
cinder-lake-crater-field.terrain_geology: Engineers dug into basaltic cinder and fired charges in sequence so the ejecta layered in the same order as on the Moon. The cinder layer is only a few feet deep, with orange-tan soil beneath.

concordia-station-dome-c.access_and_facilities: Most cargo arrives by overland traverse from Dumont d'Urville Station. The station is inaccessible in winter and needs total autonomy.
concordia-station-dome-c.climate: Polar ice cap climate, frigid all year round.

facts.label: Distance from the Geographic South Pole

concordia-station-dome-c.hazards: Extreme cold and months of complete isolation during winter.

image.author: Stephen Hudson
image.credit: Photo: Stephen Hudson, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

concordia-station-dome-c.place: Concordia Station, Dome C, Antarctic Plateau, Antarctica
concordia-station-dome-c.summary: Concordia is a French-Italian research station on the Antarctic Plateau, and it is one of the coldest places on Earth. During winter the crew is cut off from the outside world, with no transport and limited communication. That extreme isolation and confinement resembles long space missions, so the station is used for space medicine research and regularly hosts ESA scientists.
concordia-station-dome-c.terrain_geology: The station sits on an ice dome of the Antarctic Plateau.

craters-of-the-moon-basalt.access_and_facilities: The monument lies along US highways between the towns of Arco and Carey. A single paved loop road and a first-come campground serve visitors, and the loop road closes to cars in late November because of snow.
craters-of-the-moon-basalt.climate: Dry and cold at altitude, with snowy winters and hot summers. Dark lava surfaces get much hotter than the air in summer.

facts.label: Craters of the Moon lava field area

craters-of-the-moon-basalt.hazards: No backcountry water, sharp lava and loose rock in caves, and extreme summer heat and winter cold.

image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.

craters-of-the-moon-basalt.place: Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve, Idaho, USA
craters-of-the-moon-basalt.summary: Craters of the Moon is a large basaltic lava field on the Snake River Plain in central Idaho. Apollo astronauts trained there to find and collect rock samples in a harsh, unfamiliar setting. In its first field deployment, NASA's BASALT research programme ran simulated spacewalks on the lava flows as an analog for present-day Mars.
craters-of-the-moon-basalt.terrain_geology: Three lava fields along the Great Rift, with basalt flows, cinder cones, lava tubes, tree molds and deep open rift cracks.

craters-of-the-moon-national-monument.access_and_facilities: Highways cross the northwest corner. One paved loop road serves the monument, with a visitor center at its entrance and a campground. The loop road closes to traffic in late November because of snow.
craters-of-the-moon-national-monument.climate: Cold, semi-dry winters with heavy snow and warm summers.
craters-of-the-moon-national-monument.hazards: There is no backcountry water, lava is sharp, cave entrances need scrambling, and the area is dormant rather than extinct.

craters-of-the-moon-national-monument.place: Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve, Idaho, USA
craters-of-the-moon-national-monument.summary: Craters of the Moon is a large basaltic lava field in south-central Idaho with cinder cones, lava flows and lava tubes in one area. Apollo astronauts trained there to find and collect rock samples. The source also notes that the Moon's craters are mostly from impacts while these formed by eruptions, so the match is partial.
craters-of-the-moon-national-monument.terrain_geology: The lava field is the largest mostly Holocene basaltic field in the contiguous United States, built along a long volcanic rift with many cones and a long lava tube.

cuatro-cienegas.access_and_facilities: The town of Cuatro Cienegas is the municipal seat, and the basin is a biosphere reserve with a protected flora and fauna area inside it.
cuatro-cienegas.climate: The area is a desert with little rain, and water stress may grow as rainfall falls and evaporation rises.

image.author: Cazadordemolinos
image.credit: Photo: Cazadordemolinos, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Poza Azul, Cuatro Cienegas

cuatro-cienegas.summary: Cuatro Cienegas is a desert basin with hundreds of spring-fed pools, gypsum soils and stromatolites. NASA-linked studies treat its microbial mats and desert aquatic habitats as a way to think about early Mars, and NASA Earth Observatory notes that it is gypsum-rich like the sediment mound at Gale crater. Researchers link its microbial diversity to a shortage of phosphorus.
cuatro-cienegas.terrain_geology: The basin holds gypsum-rich soils and dunes, springs, pools and marshes at the eastern edge of the Chihuahuan Desert.

dallol.access_and_facilities: Travel guides say the Danakil Depression cannot be visited independently, and escorts and permits are needed.
dallol.climate: The area is among the driest and hottest on the planet, and it is one of the lowest land points on Earth.
dallol.hazards: The springs discharge very hot, strongly acidic brines, and the vents release carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulfide and sulfur dioxide.

image.author: Jan Markiewicz
image.credit: Photo: Jan Markiewicz, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Salt geyser at Dallol

dallol.place: Dallol hydrothermal system, Danakil Depression, Afar region, Ethiopia
dallol.summary: Dallol is a hydrothermal system around a small volcano in the Danakil Depression of Ethiopia. It is known for strange colours and mineral patterns and for some of the most acidic spring fluids on Earth. Researchers call it a poly-extreme site and a key system for astrobiology, because acid, salt and heat occur together.
dallol.terrain_geology: Basaltic magma pushed into old salt deposits and built a salt dome with hot springs, small geysers and salt canyons. Iron and other impurities give the surface its yellow, ochre and brown colours.

dasht-e-lut-kalut-yardang-field.access_and_facilities: The desert is a World Heritage Site. The sources read here give no access routes or facilities.
dasht-e-lut-kalut-yardang-field.climate: The desert is extremely dry and very hot, and satellite instruments have measured some of the highest ground-surface temperatures on Earth there. There are no permanent weather stations inside it.
dasht-e-lut-kalut-yardang-field.hazards: Extreme surface heat and the lack of weather stations make conditions hard to predict.

image.title: Kaluts in Lut Desert, Kavire Lut, Iran

dasht-e-lut-kalut-yardang-field.place: Dasht-e Lut (Lut Desert), Kerman and Sistan-Baluchestan provinces, southeastern Iran
dasht-e-lut-kalut-yardang-field.summary: The Lut Desert is a large salt desert in southeastern Iran with some of the largest wind-carved ridges (yardangs, locally called kaluts) on Earth. Published remote-sensing work compares its yardangs and its ripple-like dunes (transverse aeolian ridges) with those on Mars. No field campaign for planetary operations is described in the sources read here.
dasht-e-lut-kalut-yardang-field.terrain_geology: More than half the surface is volcanic rock, with parallel ridges and furrows in the centre and very tall dunes in the southeast. Mega-yardangs are easy to pick out on satellite images and run in line with a strong regional wind.

death-valley-ubehebe-crater-and-basin-fl.access_and_facilities: The craters are inside Death Valley National Park and open to visitors, a long drive from Furnace Creek and Las Vegas.

facts.label: Number of craters in the field

death-valley-ubehebe-crater-and-basin-fl.hazards: The risk of renewed volcanic activity is low.

image.author: Nomdeploom
image.credit: Photo: Nomdeploom, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

death-valley-ubehebe-crater-and-basin-fl.place: Ubehebe Crater and the basin floor, Death Valley National Park, California, USA
death-valley-ubehebe-crater-and-basin-fl.summary: Northern Death Valley has a volcanic crater field and a salt pan in one national park. NASA has used Death Valley as a Mars analog since it prepared for the Viking missions. Ubehebe Crater has been compared to Gale Crater, and researchers study the salt pan as a model for salt deposits that may have formed on Mars as water disappeared.
death-valley-ubehebe-crater-and-basin-fl.terrain_geology: Ubehebe is a maar, a crater formed by a steam-driven eruption, ringed by a tuff deposit with black ash on the rim. A playa lake lies on the crater floor.

dhofar-desert-amadee-18.access_and_facilities: Salalah, the governorate capital, has an international airport and a large seaport. Oman signed an agreement with the Austrian Space Forum to host the mission.
dhofar-desert-amadee-18.climate: The governorate has a tropical climate with a summer monsoon season called the khareef, and winters can bring dust storms.
dhofar-desert-amadee-18.hazards: Winter dust storms and sudden temperature drops from northern winds.

image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, VIIRS true colour, one day in 2023, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Dhofar desert (AMADEE-18), centred on the listed coordinates (VIIRS true colour, one day in 2023)

dhofar-desert-amadee-18.place: Dhofar desert near Marmul, Dhofar Governorate, Oman
dhofar-desert-amadee-18.summary: The Austrian Space Forum ran its AMADEE Mars simulation in the Dhofar desert in southern Oman, with a field camp near the Marmul outpost. The mission tested engineering, surface operations, astrobiology, geology and life science experiments. Reports say the terrain resembles several Martian surface features, including sedimentary structures and salt domes.
dhofar-desert-amadee-18.terrain_geology: Desert plain below a semicircle of mountains, with sedimentary structures and salt domes reported at the field site.

don-juan-pond.access_and_facilities: The nearest listed settlement is Vanda Station, to the east.

facts.label: Lowest temperature it can stay liquid

don-juan-pond.place: Don Juan Pond, Wright Valley, Victoria Land, Antarctica
don-juan-pond.summary: Don Juan Pond is a very small, extremely salty pond at the western end of Wright Valley in the Antarctic Dry Valleys. Its calcium chloride brine stays liquid at very low temperatures, which is why it is studied for what brines could do on Mars. The source read says research here may inform study of similar saline settings on other bodies.
don-juan-pond.terrain_geology: The pond sits between the Asgard and Dais ranges, ringed by salt crusts left as water evaporated. Researchers debate whether its brine comes from shallow deliquescence or from deep groundwater.

dumont-dunes.access_and_facilities: The site is reached from the state highway north of Baker and is a federal off-highway vehicle recreation area run by the Bureau of Land Management.
dumont-dunes.climate: The low elevation makes spring and summer warm to extremely hot.

image.author: Doc Searls
image.credit: Photo: Doc Searls, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Dumont Dunes, California

dumont-dunes.place: Dumont Dunes, Mojave Desert, California, United States
dumont-dunes.summary: Dumont Dunes is a field of large sand dunes in the Mojave Desert. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory drove Scarecrow, a stripped-down twin of the Curiosity rover, here to prepare for sand-trap driving in Gale crater. More recently the laboratory used it as a secondary site for drone navigation tests aimed at future Mars rotorcraft.
dumont-dunes.terrain_geology: The dunes sit beside the slow Amargosa River and are bordered by steep volcanic hills.

dunhuang-yardang-national-geopark.access_and_facilities: The geopark lies north-west of the town of Dunhuang. The sources checked give the distance but no route or visitor details.

facts.label: Distance north-west of Dunhuang town centre
Time for the formations to develop

dunhuang-yardang-national-geopark.place: Dunhuang Yardang National Geopark, Gansu province, China
dunhuang-yardang-national-geopark.summary: This geopark in Gansu province holds the largest field of yardangs in China. Yardangs are ridges that wind carves from soft rock, and they also occur on a very large scale on Mars. The sources checked here do not describe Mars analog fieldwork at this park, so the link is the landform type, not a documented programme.
dunhuang-yardang-national-geopark.terrain_geology: Wind and rain have eroded the soft ground and left harder rock standing as ridges, many named for the shapes they resemble. The formations took a very long time to develop.

el-tatio-geyser-field.access_and_facilities: A regional road links the field to San Pedro de Atacama, and unpaved roads lead into it. The local Atacameno community administers the site, which is a major tourist destination.
el-tatio-geyser-field.climate: Air is cold and thin, with large day to night swings, and most rain falls in the summer months. Wind and ultraviolet exposure are strong.

facts.label: Distance north of San Pedro de Atacama
Arsenic in hot spring water (up to)

el-tatio-geyser-field.hazards: Hot spring water carries very high arsenic, the pool edges have acidic mud, and an old well blew out in a steam column in a past year.

image.credit: Photo: Alexarje, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: El Tatio geothermal field in Chile

el-tatio-geyser-field.place: El Tatio geyser field, Antofagasta Region, Andes of northern Chile
el-tatio-geyser-field.summary: El Tatio is a high-altitude geothermal field with geysers, hot springs and silica sinter deposits in the Andes of northern Chile. It is the largest geyser field in the Southern Hemisphere. Scientists use it as an analogue for early Earth and possible past life on Mars, and its low air pressure and strong ultraviolet light are cited as Mars-like conditions.
el-tatio-geyser-field.terrain_geology: The field lies at the western foot of a line of stratovolcanoes on the Chile and Bolivia border. Its silica sinter holds microbial textures, and microstructures in the Columbia Hills at the Home Plate landform on Mars resemble biogenic structures found at El Tatio, though the source notes this does not mean the Martian ones are biogenic.

emi-koussi-volcano-tibesti.access_and_facilities: The region is remote and access is difficult for political reasons. Dirt roads cross the western and eastern margins of the summit caldera.
emi-koussi-volcano-tibesti.climate: Desert mountain climate. No weather stations are close to the summit, so rainfall there is estimated from cloud cover.

facts.label: Estimated annual precipitation near the summit

emi-koussi-volcano-tibesti.hazards: Volcanism in the area is poorly studied, and fumarole and hot spring activity continues.

emi-koussi-volcano-tibesti.place: Emi Koussi, Tibesti Mountains, Borkou Region, Chad
emi-koussi-volcano-tibesti.summary: Emi Koussi is a large shield volcano at the southeast end of the Tibesti Mountains and the highest mountain in the Sahara. Two nested calderas cap it, and a smaller caldera called Era Kohor holds sodium carbonate deposits. It has been studied as an analogue of the Martian volcano Elysium Mons. This comparison is a candidate in our screening and is not in our reference list.
emi-koussi-volcano-tibesti.terrain_geology: Alkaline lavas, ignimbrites, lava domes, cinder cones and maars cover the volcano. The floor of Era Kohor is white with sodium carbonate and holds a salt lake. Fumaroles and hot springs are still active at the southern foot.

erfoud-merzouga-mars2013.access_and_facilities: Merzouga is a village with hotels and restaurants for visitors, a short drive from Erfoud and Rissani. Mission support during the simulation was run from Innsbruck, Austria.
erfoud-merzouga-mars2013.hazards: Flash floods struck Merzouga in an earlier year and displaced many residents.

image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.

erfoud-merzouga-mars2013.place: Erfoud and Merzouga, Errachidia Province, Draa-Tafilalet, Morocco
erfoud-merzouga-mars2013.summary: Erfoud is an oasis town on the Saharan edge of Morocco, close to the Erg Chebbi dunes at Merzouga. The Austrian Space Forum ran a month-long Mars analog field simulation near Erfoud, including work at the Kess Kess formation, a set of old mud mound structures. Wikipedia notes that the terrain around Erfoud is used for Mars analog research.
erfoud-merzouga-mars2013.terrain_geology: Desert edge with large Erg Chebbi dunes, and the Kess Kess mud mound structures of Devonian age near Erfoud.

esa-caves-site-sa-grutta-sardinia.access_and_facilities: The course starts with a preparation week and then moves underground, where the team sets up a basecamp in the cave.

esa-caves-site-sa-grutta-sardinia.place: Sa Grutta cave, Supramonte, Sardinia, Italy
esa-caves-site-sa-grutta-sardinia.summary: ESA CAVES is an astronaut training course held underground in the Supramonte area of Sardinia, with the Sa Grutta cave used as basecamp. ESA describes caves as a space analog for working in teams where safety is critical, and the course is as much about teamwork as technical caving. Crews have included astronauts from several space agencies. The sources read do not describe the cave as a lava tube.

fiskenaesset-anorthosite-complex-qeqerta.access_and_facilities: The nearest settlement is Qeqertarsuatsiaat, also called Fiskenaesset, on an island off the Labrador Sea coast.

fiskenaesset-anorthosite-complex-qeqerta.place: Fiskenaesset anorthosite complex, near Qeqertarsuatsiaat (Fiskenaesset), Sermersooq municipality, southwestern Greenland
fiskenaesset-anorthosite-complex-qeqerta.summary: The Fiskenaesset complex is a metamorphosed layered intrusion that is rich in anorthosite. Older studies found similarities between its plagioclase and lunar plagioclase, but also differences, and an older Greenland geological survey report cautioned against drawing planetary conclusions from the comparison. A recent conference abstract reports a pink spinel rock there that matches lunar spinel in composition and texture; that abstract has not been peer reviewed in the sources we found.
fiskenaesset-anorthosite-complex-qeqerta.terrain_geology: Anorthosite occurs as conformable layers within high-grade gneisses.

fukushima-robot-test-field-lunar-analog-.access_and_facilities: The field sits in the Minamisoma reconstruction industrial park and was built under the Fukushima Innovation Coast Framework. The university plans to open the lunar analog area to potential users.

image.author: NASA GIBS
image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Fukushima Robot Test Field lunar analog ('Moon/Mars Garden'), centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

fukushima-robot-test-field-lunar-analog-.place: Fukushima Robot Test Field, Minamisoma, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan
fukushima-robot-test-field-lunar-analog-.summary: The Fukushima Robot Test Field is a facility in Minamisoma for testing robots on land, at sea and in the air. The University of Aizu has built a simulated lunar crater there as part of its Moon/Mars Garden concept, to test robot movement and communication. The organisers plan to open it to outside users as a testbed.
fukushima-robot-test-field-lunar-analog-.terrain_geology: The lunar area is a built crater covered with a lunar soil analogue, not a natural geological feature.

gilf-kebir-plateau-and-wadis.access_and_facilities: The plateau lies inside Gilf Kebir National Park. The sources read here give no road, station or permit details.
gilf-kebir-plateau-and-wadis.climate: The climate is extremely hyperarid, with rainfall that barely registers over a year. July days are the hottest and January nights the coolest.

image.author: Clemens Schmillen
image.credit: Photo: Clemens Schmillen, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: View from the Gilf Kebir ridge south into Wadi Sura

gilf-kebir-plateau-and-wadis.place: Gilf Kebir plateau, Western Desert, southwest Egypt
gilf-kebir-plateau-and-wadis.summary: Gilf Kebir is a large sandstone plateau in the Libyan Desert of southwest Egypt, cut by dry seasonal valleys called wadis. A NASA technical report used landforms in southwest Egypt as a basis for comparison with Mars. The sources read here do not describe a modern analog field campaign at the plateau itself.
gilf-kebir-plateau-and-wadis.terrain_geology: The plateau is sandstone and rises well above the surrounding desert floor, with wadis crossing it. The only way up from the southern plains is the Aqaba Pass.

gosses-bluff-crater.access_and_facilities: The site lies in the Tnorala Conservation Reserve, west of Alice Springs. It is a sacred place to the Western Arrernte.

image.author: NASA/ISS Expedition 7 crew member
image.credit: Photo: NASA/ISS Expedition 7 crew member, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Gosses Bluff, Northern Territory, from the International Space Station

gosses-bluff-crater.place: Gosses Bluff (Tnorala), Tnorala Conservation Reserve, Northern Territory, Australia
gosses-bluff-crater.summary: Gosses Bluff, known as Tnorala to the Western Arrernte people, is the eroded remnant of an impact crater in central Australia. The ring of hills seen today is the exposed central uplift of a much larger original crater. Our reference list uses it as an analog for central-peak structure on the Moon, but we did not find a source that describes it as a lunar analog.
gosses-bluff-crater.terrain_geology: The ridge is made of fractured and brecciated sandstone and shale. Shatter cones are the strongest evidence of an impact origin.

grand-canyon-south-rim-and-inner-canyon.access_and_facilities: Grand Canyon Village on the South Rim has hotels, including El Tovar, and a railway station.
grand-canyon-south-rim-and-inner-canyon.climate: The inner gorge is hot in summer, while the rims have cold winters with heavy snow. The South Rim is drier than the North Rim.
grand-canyon-south-rim-and-inner-canyon.hazards: Dehydration, heat, hypothermia, winter storms, summer thunderstorms and rockfall.

image.title: Satellite view of Grand Canyon (South Rim and inner canyon), centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

grand-canyon-south-rim-and-inner-canyon.place: Grand Canyon, South Rim and inner canyon, Arizona, USA
grand-canyon-south-rim-and-inner-canyon.summary: The Grand Canyon is a very deep gorge cut by the Colorado River through thick rock layers. Apollo astronauts took geology field trips here in the early years of the programme to learn to read rock layers. The canyon is geologically very different from the Moon, so it is a training site more than a surface look-alike.
grand-canyon-south-rim-and-inner-canyon.terrain_geology: Stacked sedimentary layers on the rim, such as the Kaibab Limestone, above very old schist at the bottom of the inner gorge.

harrat-khaybar-and-umm-jirsan-lava-tube.place: Harrat Khaybar and Umm Jirsan lava tube, Hejaz region, Saudi Arabia
harrat-khaybar-and-umm-jirsan-lava-tube.summary: Harrat Khaybar is a large field of basaltic lava north of Medina in Saudi Arabia, with cinder cones, lava flows and the country's longest known lava tube system, Umm Jirsan. The sources read describe its geology and archaeology but do not describe it as an analog site. Its place on our list is a GSOP screening result, a candidate not in our reference list.
harrat-khaybar-and-umm-jirsan-lava-tube.terrain_geology: Lava has erupted along a long north-south line of vents, with pale comendite domes in the White Mountains and darker hawaiite flows elsewhere. Jabal Qidr is a scoria cone listed among IUGS geological heritage sites.

haughton-crater-devon-island.access_and_facilities: The site is remote, and the project runs a research station on the island each summer.
haughton-crater-devon-island.climate: Temperatures stay below freezing for much of the year, and weathering is slow. Devon Island is far milder than Mars.

image.author: Denni
image.credit: Radar image: Denni, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Radar image of Haughton impact crater, Devon Island

haughton-crater-devon-island.place: Haughton impact crater, Devon Island, Nunavut, Canada
haughton-crater-devon-island.summary: Haughton is an impact crater on Devon Island in the Canadian High Arctic. The Haughton-Mars Project, run by SETI and the Mars Institute and funded mainly by NASA, uses the crater and surrounding terrain as a planetary analog, in particular for the Moon and Mars. The Mars Institute describes Devon Island as the largest continuous area of barren rocky polar desert on Earth.
haughton-crater-devon-island.terrain_geology: The impact peeled back shale and siltstone to expose the gneissic basement, and material from deep below the surface has been identified. Valley networks, canyons, gullies and old lake beds surround the crater.

haughton-crater-hmp-and-fmars.access_and_facilities: The project base has stood at its present location since early in the century. The sources checked do not describe how the site is reached.
haughton-crater-hmp-and-fmars.climate: At this latitude temperatures stay below freezing for much of the year. The Mars Institute calls Devon Island the largest continuous area of barren rocky polar desert on Earth.

image.author: Brian Shiro
image.credit: Photo: Brian Shiro, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: FMARS habitat, Devon Island

haughton-crater-hmp-and-fmars.place: Haughton impact crater, Devon Island, Nunavut, Canada
haughton-crater-hmp-and-fmars.summary: Haughton is an impact crater on Devon Island in the Canadian Arctic. The Haughton-Mars Project, run by the Mars Institute and the SETI Institute with NASA support, uses the crater to test the challenges of living and working on Mars. The Mars Society also operates the Flashline Mars Arctic Research Station at the crater.
haughton-crater-hmp-and-fmars.terrain_geology: The impact removed much of the shale and siltstone and exposed the older basement rock, and the crater centre holds impact breccia that is frozen with permafrost. Cold and slow weathering keep features that craters at lower latitudes lose.

henbury-craters.access_and_facilities: The reserve lies southwest of Alice Springs and is managed by the Northern Territory parks authority. Research needs permission from that authority, and Aboriginal heritage issues may apply.

image.title: Henbury Meteorite Crater

henbury-craters.place: Henbury Meteorites Conservation Reserve, southwest of Alice Springs, Northern Territory, Australia
henbury-craters.summary: Henbury is a cluster of small, closely spaced impact craters formed when an iron meteorite broke up before it hit the ground. The Mars Society Australia lists it among its planetary analogue sites and notes that the craters were studied to give context to the Apollo program. It is a protected reserve, so field work needs permission.
henbury-craters.terrain_geology: The craters formed in desert ground from the fall of iron-nickel meteorite fragments, and several tonnes of those fragments have been recovered. Studies of crater erosion and infill are described as having analogue value.

hi-seas-habitat-mauna-loa.access_and_facilities: The habitat is a two-floor dome with an attached shipping container that holds supplies, water and power systems.
hi-seas-habitat-mauna-loa.hazards: The altitude slightly raises radiation exposure, and one mission was halted after a crew member suffered an electric shock.

hi-seas-habitat-mauna-loa.place: HI-SEAS habitat, Mauna Loa, Island of Hawaii, USA
hi-seas-habitat-mauna-loa.summary: HI-SEAS is a small dome habitat on the slope of Mauna Loa where crews of six lived in isolation for simulated Mars missions. NASA's Human Research Program funded follow-up studies for several years, and the site is now operated by the International MoonBase Alliance. The sources we read describe the area as isolated with Mars-like features.
hi-seas-habitat-mauna-loa.terrain_geology: A barren volcanic slope far from other buildings, described as having Mars-like features.

holuhraun-lava-field.access_and_facilities: An unnumbered track crosses the field and joins a gravel highland road at both ends.
holuhraun-lava-field.hazards: Glacial outburst floods have repeatedly affected the area.

holuhraun-lava-field.place: Holuhraun lava field, Icelandic Highlands, Iceland
holuhraun-lava-field.summary: Holuhraun is a basaltic lava field just north of the Vatnajokull ice cap in the Icelandic Highlands. It grew in a recent fissure eruption (dates in the facts), so much of it is very fresh. The page read gives no Mars or Moon analog statements, so the analog case here comes from GSOP's reference list rather than from that source.
holuhraun-lava-field.terrain_geology: Lava lies at the southern end of the Odadahraun lava desert, with the Dyngjujokull outlet glacier immediately to the south and the Askja caldera to the north.

hopi-buttes-volcanic-field.access_and_facilities: The field lies mostly on the Navajo Reservation, north of Holbrook.

image.author: John Fowler
image.credit: Photo: John Fowler, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Hopi Buttes, Arizona

hopi-buttes-volcanic-field.place: Hopi Buttes volcanic field, near Dilkon, Navajo Nation, northeastern Arizona, United States
hopi-buttes-volcanic-field.summary: The Hopi Buttes are a field of small volcanoes on the Colorado Plateau. In the years before the first lunar landing, USGS and NASA personnel tested early Apollo spacesuits and a lunar flying vehicle here. It was one of several nearby volcanic sites visited during Apollo preparation, and the sources we found do not rank it above Cinder Lake or Sunset Crater for crater training.
hopi-buttes-volcanic-field.terrain_geology: The field has about three hundred maars and diatremes. Eastern parts show shallowly eroded maar deposits, and western parts show deeper-eroded feeder diatremes.

huailai-lunar-landing-test-site.access_and_facilities: It is a restricted aerospace facility. One report says it is run by the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation. Details of the site are only partly published.

huailai-lunar-landing-test-site.place: Extraterrestrial landing test site, Huailai County, Hebei province, China
huailai-lunar-landing-test-site.summary: This is China's test facility for landing spacecraft on other bodies, in Huailai County, Hebei. It uses tall tether towers to reduce the load on a lander, which mimics low gravity, and a cratered field to mimic rough terrain. It was used for a Mars lander hover and obstacle test and, more recently, for a landing and takeoff test of the Lanyue crewed lunar lander.
huailai-lunar-landing-test-site.terrain_geology: The field is a built test area with craters and tether towers, not a natural analog.

isro-challakere-lunar-terrain-test-facil.access_and_facilities: Challakere is in a science township in Chitradurga district that is shared by ISRO, DRDO, IISc and BARC. Other scientific and strategic agencies also hold land there.
isro-challakere-lunar-terrain-test-facil.climate: Semi-arid tropical; hot, with monsoon rains.

image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of ISRO Challakere lunar terrain test facility, centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

isro-challakere-lunar-terrain-test-facil.summary: At Challakere, ISRO's satellite centre made artificial craters so the terrain would resemble the lunar surface, and used them to test the landing sensors of ISRO's second lunar lander. A small ISRO aircraft carrying the sensors flew over the craters several times. This is a built test site for sensor and landing tests, not a natural terrain.
isro-challakere-lunar-terrain-test-facil.terrain_geology: Dug and shaped craters on flat granitic-gneiss terrain covered with simulant soil.

kamchatka-lunokhod-chassis-trials-tolbac.place: Tolbachik volcano area, Kamchatka Peninsula, Russia
kamchatka-lunokhod-chassis-trials-tolbac.summary: Tolbachik is a basaltic volcanic complex on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia's Far East. A Brown University presentation lists tests in Kamchatka among the Lunokhod rover test activities, and a travel blog says the Soviets tested their first lunar rover at Tolbachik. The Planetary Society also reported that ash from earlier eruptions was good for testing Mars rover mobility. We did not find a primary Soviet-era source for the lunar tests at this exact spot.
kamchatka-lunokhod-chassis-trials-tolbac.terrain_geology: The volcano produced a large basaltic fissure eruption that built several cinder cones, and a later eruption left lava caves. Fumarole deposits are a source of rare minerals.

kamil-crater.access_and_facilities: The crater is very remote and lies close to the Sudan border. A geophysical expedition reached it for fieldwork.

image.author: NASA GIBS
image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Kamil crater, centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

kamil-crater.place: Kamil crater, East Uweinat Desert, New Valley Governorate, Egypt
kamil-crater.summary: Kamil is a small, young impact crater in the far southwest of Egypt, close to the Sudan border. It has a well-preserved ray system, which Wikipedia describes as rare among craters on Earth. It was located on satellite imagery and later confirmed on the ground; we found no source calling it an established Moon analog, and GSOP lists it as a candidate not in our reference list.
kamil-crater.terrain_geology: An iron meteorite struck sandstone bedrock, and sand now covers part of the crater. Thousands of meteorite fragments were collected.

karakul-impact-structure-pamir.access_and_facilities: A small village of the same name lies on the eastern shore, and the area is inside Tajik National Park.

image.author: NASA (Landsat 7)
image.credit: Photo: NASA (Landsat 7), Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

karakul-impact-structure-pamir.place: Karakul impact structure and lake, Pamir Mountains, Tajikistan
karakul-impact-structure-pamir.summary: Karakul is a large, brackish lake that fills an impact crater high in the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan. The crater is young in geological terms, though its age is still uncertain. The sources read do not describe it as an analog site, so its place on our list is a GSOP screening result, a candidate not in our reference list.
karakul-impact-structure-pamir.terrain_geology: The lake has no outlet and is surrounded mostly by pasture, with marshes, wet meadows and pebbly and sandy plains.

kaunertal-glacier-amadee-15.access_and_facilities: A toll road runs up the valley to the base of the glacier ski area, and the base station sat near the end of it.

kaunertal-glacier-amadee-15.summary: The Austrian Space Forum ran a two-week Mars simulation on the Kaunertal Glacier (dates are in the facts). Analog astronauts in Aouda spacesuit simulators worked with robotic vehicles under a mission support center in Innsbruck. The forum chose the site for its access and its small-scale terrain resembling Mars where water ice is present, and describes it as the highest-altitude analog mission it has run (a claim by the organizers).
kaunertal-glacier-amadee-15.terrain_geology: The site is a rock glacier and glacier in the Alps, studied with ground-penetrating radar and glacier microbial life detection.

kilauea-caldera-and-ka-u-desert.access_and_facilities: Both areas are in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, which has one hotel and restaurant inside it. Parts of the park close during high volcanic activity.
kilauea-caldera-and-ka-u-desert.climate: The Kaʻū Desert gets more than a metre of rain a year, so it is not a true desert, and the rain turns acidic when it mixes with volcanic sulfur dioxide.

facts.label: Ka'u Desert annual rainfall, more than

kilauea-caldera-and-ka-u-desert.hazards: Hazards include volcanic gas, acid rain, ash, explosions and lava; the park closes areas when gas blows toward them.

kilauea-caldera-and-ka-u-desert.place: Kilauea summit caldera and Kaʻū Desert, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Hawaiʻi, USA
kilauea-caldera-and-ka-u-desert.summary: Kilauea is an active basaltic volcano on the island of Hawaiʻi, and the Kaʻū Desert lies on its south-west flank. NASA used the area to train Apollo astronauts to recognise volcanic features, plan traverses, collect samples and take photographs. Astronauts from several Apollo landing missions used this training on the Moon.
kilauea-caldera-and-ka-u-desert.terrain_geology: The Kaʻū Desert surface is dried lava remnants, volcanic ash, sand and gravel. The summit caldera holds a pit crater called Halemaʻumaʻu.

kilauea-ka-u-desert-basalt.access_and_facilities: Access and permits through the national park strongly shaped which sites were chosen. Some trail sites must be kept away from tourist traffic.
kilauea-ka-u-desert-basalt.climate: The summit area is mild and wet, with rain or sun on any given day and no snow.
kilauea-ka-u-desert-basalt.hazards: The volcano is active, rim collapses at the caldera have likely compromised one study site, and fumarole areas have hot, acidic gas.

kilauea-ka-u-desert-basalt.place: Kilauea summit region (including the Ka'u Desert), Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Hawaii, USA
kilauea-ka-u-desert-basalt.summary: Kilauea is an active shield volcano whose basalt terrain hosted fieldwork for the BASALT program, a NASA-funded study of how astronauts might work on Mars. The program chose Hawaii and Idaho because both have volcanic terrain similar to Mars, and it ran simulated missions with delayed communications. The Hawaii sites are treated as analogs for wetter and more volcanically active periods of early Mars.
kilauea-ka-u-desert-basalt.terrain_geology: Hawaiian lavas are mostly primitive basalt, with low-relief ropy and vesicular flows at Mauna Ulu and a lava lake at Kilauea Iki. Several of these lava types match compositions found by Mars rovers and in meteorites.

kilbourne-hole-and-potrillo-volcanic-fie.access_and_facilities: The hole is in Organ Mountains-Desert Peaks National Monument, reached by a county road west of the railroad. Much land inside the hole is private, and collecting rocks is illegal.

kilbourne-hole-and-potrillo-volcanic-fie.place: Kilbourne Hole, Potrillo volcanic field, Dona Ana County, New Mexico, USA
kilbourne-hole-and-potrillo-volcanic-fie.summary: Kilbourne Hole is a maar, a volcanic crater formed by a steam-driven eruption, in the Potrillo volcanic field of southern New Mexico. NASA trained Apollo astronauts in lunar geology here, and a later NASA field team tested instruments for future missions and simulated moonwalks in the hole.
kilbourne-hole-and-potrillo-volcanic-fie.terrain_geology: The rim cliffs are basalt with clear columnar jointing, and the ejecta holds many fragments of mantle and lower crust rock. Sand dunes sit on the east side, and a dry lakebed lies on the crater floor.

kolyma-lowland-permafrost.climate: Subarctic. We found no temperature or rainfall figures in the sources we read.

facts.label: Largest reported thaw subsidence in northeast Siberia

kolyma-lowland-permafrost.hazards: Ice-rich permafrost can sink badly when it thaws.

kolyma-lowland-permafrost.summary: The Kolyma Lowland is a flat plain of marshes and lakes in northeast Siberia with a subarctic climate. Its ice-rich Pleistocene permafrost, known as Yedoma, holds well-preserved organic matter, fossils and ancient DNA. We did not find a source that calls it a Mars analog; GSOP lists it as a reference for life preserved in ground ice.
kolyma-lowland-permafrost.terrain_geology: A lowland plain between the Alazeya and Yukagir plateaus, with thick fine-grained, ice-rich permafrost deposits.

kumtag-desert-yutu-rover-tests-dunhuang.access_and_facilities: A news report placed the rover tests in the desert some distance from Dunhuang city.
kumtag-desert-yutu-rover-tests-dunhuang.climate: Winds blow mostly from the west and northwest, and some scrubby plants get water only once in several years.

facts.label: Rover test site distance from Dunhuang (2011 report)

kumtag-desert-yutu-rover-tests-dunhuang.place: Kumtag Desert, near Dunhuang, Gansu and Xinjiang, China
kumtag-desert-yutu-rover-tests-dunhuang.summary: Kumtag is a large sandy desert in northwestern China that borders Dunhuang. News reports say China tested its Yutu lunar rover in this desert before launch, and an official said it was the most suitable of the deserts surveyed. The rover later landed on ground that was rougher than the test terrain.
kumtag-desert-yutu-rover-tests-dunhuang.terrain_geology: Drift-sand dunes can be very tall along the desert ranges, and the southern rim is a maze of hills.

kutch-matanomadh-jarosite.access_and_facilities: The site is northwest of Bhuj in Kutch.
kutch-matanomadh-jarosite.climate: The mineral assemblage is consistent with an oxidizing environment and periodic shifts between humid and arid conditions.

kutch-matanomadh-jarosite.summary: A team from SAC-ISRO, IIT Kharagpur and NGRI reported jarosite near Matanomadh (first report year in the facts) and argued the setting resembles Martian jarosite sites. A later paper in American Mineralogist identified the mineral as natrojarosite, the sodium variant. It reports natrojarosite and associated sulfates that point to acidic, water-limited conditions, which the authors call analogous to the Noachian-Hesperian period of Mars.
kutch-matanomadh-jarosite.terrain_geology: The area is a basalt-hosted setting in the Palaeocene Matanomadh Formation, with natrojarosite, natroalunite, kaolinite and anhydrite.

ladakh-tso-kar-and-puga.access_and_facilities: The Leh to Manali road passes west of the lake, and roads from Miru reach its shores. A tented camp stands on the west bank.
ladakh-tso-kar-and-puga.climate: Winters are extreme and summers are warm with large daily swings. Rain and snow are very rare, and the basin sits in a rain shadow.

facts.label: Distance of Leh to Manali road west of lake

ladakh-tso-kar-and-puga.hazards: Extreme cold, thin air and strong ultraviolet radiation.

ladakh-tso-kar-and-puga.place: Tso Kar basin and Puga Valley, Rupshu, Changthang, Ladakh, India
ladakh-tso-kar-and-puga.summary: Tso Kar is a high-altitude salt lake in the Changthang region of southern Ladakh. Researchers have studied Puga hot spring deposits and Tso Kar brine together as possible Mars analogs. ISRO and Protoplanet built the HOPE analog station at Tso Kar to simulate Moon and Mars conditions.
ladakh-tso-kar-and-puga.terrain_geology: Tso Kar has no outflow, and the evaporating saline water leaves white salt crusts along its margins. At Puga, spectroscopy has found borate minerals with halite and opaline silica, and sulfate minerals alongside crystalline sulfur.

lake-abbe-hydrothermal-carbonate-chimney.access_and_facilities: The area is described as one of the most inaccessible on Earth. The sources read here name no road or station details.
lake-abbe-hydrothermal-carbonate-chimney.climate: The climate is hot, dry and sunny all year, with summer temperatures in the thirties and forties.
lake-abbe-hydrothermal-carbonate-chimney.hazards: Lake level swings sharply with small climate changes, and the surroundings are very hot.

lake-abbe-hydrothermal-carbonate-chimney.place: Lake Abbe (Abhe Bad), Afar Depression, on the Djibouti and Ethiopia border
lake-abbe-hydrothermal-carbonate-chimney.summary: Lake Abbe is a salt lake in the Afar Depression, where tall carbonate chimneys rise from the shore and steam comes out of them. The chimneys form where lake water mixes with hot deeper fluid. The sources read here describe the geology but do not describe any use of the site as a planetary analog.
lake-abbe-hydrothermal-carbonate-chimney.terrain_geology: Limestone (carbonate) chimneys form where hydrothermal fluid meets lake water, in alternating layers of calcite and silica-bearing calcite. The lake sits at the Afar triple junction, with a dormant volcano on its northwest shore.

lake-gilmore-acid-saline-lakes.climate: Hot, dry summers and cool winters at the nearest climate station, in Salmon Gums.

lake-gilmore-acid-saline-lakes.place: Lake Gilmore, Goldfields-Esperance region, Western Australia, Australia
lake-gilmore-acid-saline-lakes.summary: Lake Gilmore is an acidic, ephemeral salt lake in southern Western Australia. Researchers study it and similar lakes because their interbedded clays and sulfates resemble Martian geochemistry. A modeling study found that the Meridiani Planum area shares acidic saline water, sulfates and iron minerals with these lakes, with some differences.
lake-gilmore-acid-saline-lakes.terrain_geology: Acid playa sediments include clay minerals and sulfates, and the minerals jarosite and alunite occur at Lake Gilmore and two other Western Australian dry lakes.

lanzarote-timanfaya.access_and_facilities: Visitors park at a public car park and tour by coach on a road closed to private traffic. Two footpaths need prior authorisation and a guide.
lanzarote-timanfaya.hazards: Very hot ground close to the surface, and strictly controlled access to protect plants and animals.

lanzarote-timanfaya.place: Timanfaya National Park, Lanzarote, Canary Islands, Spain
lanzarote-timanfaya.summary: Timanfaya is a national park of fresh volcanic terrain on the southwest of Lanzarote. ESA has used Lanzarote for the geology course that trains astronauts for work on the Moon, Mars and asteroids. Press reports also say NASA and ESA have tested rovers on the island's lava fields.
lanzarote-timanfaya.terrain_geology: Entirely volcanic ground formed mostly by eruptions that lasted several years in the early eighteenth century, with craters, lava fields and lava tubes. Surface rock is very hot just below ground.

lanzarote-timanfaya-and-la-corona-lava-t.access_and_facilities: A car park serves a coach tour on a road otherwise closed to the public, and two footpaths need prior authorization and a guide.
lanzarote-timanfaya-and-la-corona-lava-t.hazards: The ground near the core of the park is very hot just below the surface.

lanzarote-timanfaya-and-la-corona-lava-t.place: Timanfaya National Park and La Corona lava tube, Lanzarote, Canary Islands, Spain
lanzarote-timanfaya-and-la-corona-lava-t.summary: Lanzarote is a young volcanic island, and Timanfaya National Park covers fresh basalt lava and cones from historic eruptions. ESA's PANGAEA course has used the island for years to train astronauts in field geology and astrobiology for Moon and Mars exploration, including visits to Timanfaya and the La Corona lava tube. ESA notes that underground structures such as lava tubes are good shelters from radiation.
lanzarote-timanfaya-and-la-corona-lava-t.terrain_geology: The park is made entirely of volcanic soil from large eruptions in the early eighteenth century, with the most recent activity in the early nineteenth century.

lava-beds-national-monument.access_and_facilities: Many caves have marked entrances and developed trails for the public. Lowering a rover through a skylight remains a hard problem for tube exploration.

lava-beds-national-monument.place: Lava Beds National Monument, Siskiyou and Modoc counties, northeastern California, United States
lava-beds-national-monument.summary: Lava Beds is a protected area on the flank of Medicine Lake Volcano with the highest concentration of lava caves in North America. NASA's BRAILLE project used it to practice cave exploration with a test rover called CaveR, as preparation for lunar and Martian lava tubes. Lava tubes could shelter Moon bases from radiation, and on Mars they could protect possible life.
lava-beds-national-monument.terrain_geology: The monument sits where three physiographic provinces meet and has many lava tubes, cave collapse trenches and high desert shrubland.

licancabur-volcano-summit-lake.access_and_facilities: Climbers usually approach from the Bolivian side. The town of San Pedro de Atacama lies to the west.
licancabur-volcano-summit-lake.climate: It is cold, dry and windy, with low air pressure and large swings between day and night. There are no glaciers and snow cover is temporary.

facts.label: Distance to San Pedro de Atacama

licancabur-volcano-summit-lake.hazards: It is a potentially active volcano with no known historical eruption. The upper cone is steep and unstable, and bad weather can arrive quickly.

licancabur-volcano-summit-lake.place: Licancabur volcano, Chile and Bolivia border, Central Andes
licancabur-volcano-summit-lake.summary: Licancabur is a stratovolcano on the Chile and Bolivia border. Its summit crater holds a small freshwater lake, one of the highest lakes in the world. Researchers have studied the area because conditions at its lakes resemble those believed to have existed in former Martian lakes.
licancabur-volcano-summit-lake.terrain_geology: The cone is built on older ignimbrites and is made mainly of andesite, with steep slopes from viscous lava. Lava flows reach far from the summit.

lonar-crater.access_and_facilities: The lake is a National Geological Monument and a Ramsar site, located near the town of Lonar.
lonar-crater.climate: Tropical monsoon; hot summers, wet monsoon season.

lonar-crater.place: Lonar Lake crater, Buldhana district, Maharashtra, India
lonar-crater.summary: Lonar Lake is a saline, highly alkaline lake that fills a meteorite impact crater in the Deccan Plateau of Maharashtra. Wikipedia describes it as the only terrestrial impact crater in the world formed entirely within basalt. That is why it is compared with basaltic lunar terrain, and a study by IIT Bombay reported that minerals in soil from the crater were similar to lunar rocks brought back by the Apollo missions.
lonar-crater.terrain_geology: The crater is cut into Deccan Traps basalt, with layered lava flows exposed in the crater wall and an ejecta blanket around the rim. Drill cores beneath the floor contain breccia with shatter cones, which is evidence of shock metamorphism.

lonar-crater-mars-context.access_and_facilities: The crater is next to the town of Lonar in Buldhana district.
lonar-crater-mars-context.climate: Monsoon climate with dry deciduous forest around the crater.
lonar-crater-mars-context.hazards: Farm chemicals, littering and sewage pollute the lake, and illegal logging and mining have changed the local ground.

image.title: Lonar crater panorama

lonar-crater-mars-context.place: Lonar crater, Buldhana district, Maharashtra, India
lonar-crater-mars-context.summary: Lonar is a meteorite impact crater in the flood basalt of the Deccan Traps, and it holds a saline, alkaline lake. Its ejecta layers show radial movement and forms described as similar to those seen on Mars. A university study also reported soil minerals resembling Apollo lunar rocks. It is a national geological monument and a Ramsar wetland.
lonar-crater-mars-context.terrain_geology: The host rock is Deccan basalt. The crater rim rises a little above the surrounding land, and the lake sits in a basin with no outflow.

lop-nur-great-ear-salt-crust.access_and_facilities: A provincial highway from Hami and a railway serve the area. Some parts are under military management and closed to the public.

lop-nur-great-ear-salt-crust.place: Lop Nur, Ruoqiang County, Xinjiang, China
lop-nur-great-ear-salt-crust.summary: Lop Nur is a former salt lake on the eastern edge of the Tarim Basin, between the Taklamakan and Kumtag deserts. The dry basin is covered by a thick salt crust, and satellite images show the concentric shorelines of the vanished lake. We found no source that uses it as a Mars analog; GSOP lists it as a candidate not in our reference list.
lop-nur-great-ear-salt-crust.terrain_geology: A flat, dry lake basin with a salt crust and ring-shaped old shorelines. The lake dried as water was diverted and rivers shifted.

lunar-crater-volcanic-field.access_and_facilities: Two highways pass through the field and dirt roads cross it, with parking at Easy Chair and on the rim of Lunar Crater. Tonopah is the nearest named town in the source.

lunar-crater-volcanic-field.place: Lunar Crater volcanic field, Nye County, Nevada, USA
lunar-crater-volcanic-field.summary: Lunar Crater volcanic field is a dry basaltic field in central Nevada with lava flows, scoria cones, tuff rings and four maars. Wikipedia says it has been used to test prototype Mars rovers and to train astronauts for the Moon landings. Lunar Crater itself is a National Natural Landmark.
lunar-crater-volcanic-field.terrain_geology: The field has many small volcanoes, lava flows and a near-circular maar called Lunar Crater, set around a dry lake bed.

lunodrom-simferopol-28-crimea.access_and_facilities: Sources disagree on the exact site: some name Shkolnoye (a former closed town), others the village of Shkilne northwest of Simferopol. Current access is not documented in the sources we read.

lunodrom-simferopol-28-crimea.summary: The lunodrom was a rover training track near Simferopol, built to test the Lunokhod rover frame and to train the engineers who drove it. Drivers with no earlier vehicle experience learned to control a machine on another body, allowing for signal delay. Crimea is internationally recognised as part of Ukraine but has been controlled by Russia since the annexation.
lunodrom-simferopol-28-crimea.terrain_geology: Descriptions of the course mention craters, ditches, trenches, boulders, gravel walls and sandy slopes.

makhtesh-ramon-d-mars-amadee-20.access_and_facilities: The small town of Mitzpe Ramon sits on the northern edge, and a visitor centre is run by the Israel Nature and Parks Authority. The mission crew lived in a purpose-built solar-powered habitat.

makhtesh-ramon-d-mars-amadee-20.place: Makhtesh Ramon, Negev desert, near Mitzpe Ramon, Israel
makhtesh-ramon-d-mars-amadee-20.summary: Makhtesh Ramon is a large erosional depression in Israel's Negev desert. The Austrian Space Forum, the Israel Space Agency and the Israeli group D-MARS ran an Austrian Space Forum Mars analog mission there, with a crew of six analog astronauts. Reports describe the crater's geology as similar to Mars in several respects.
makhtesh-ramon-d-mars-amadee-20.terrain_geology: The basin holds clay hills in red and yellow tones, a black basalt hill, dark intrusive rock, quartzite hills and vertical dikes. Rocks on the floor are very old, and the basin formed when rivers carved the softer rock after the Arava rift valley opened.

mars-base-1-jinchang.access_and_facilities: The nearest town is Jinchang. The base has living quarters, a control room, a greenhouse and an air lock.
mars-base-1-jinchang.climate: The climate is arid with wind all year round, with large daily and seasonal temperature swings.

mars-base-1-jinchang.place: Mars analog base near Jinchang, Gansu, China (Hexi Corridor, Gobi Desert)
mars-base-1-jinchang.summary: This is a Mars simulation and education base built by the company C-Space in barren Gobi Desert hills near Jinchang. Its core area has a master control compartment, an air-lock compartment and a crew compartment, and it is used for astronaut-style training and public education. The founder said the site was chosen because its landform is the closest match to Mars that the team could find on Earth, while a Peking University professor said the building and desert are not representative of the hostile conditions on Mars.
mars-base-1-jinchang.terrain_geology: The wider area is higher in the south and lower in the north, alternating between Gobi Desert and mountain areas.

mars-desert-research-station-hanksville.access_and_facilities: The station is northwest of Hanksville by road. Crews reach field destinations on foot or by all-terrain vehicle.
mars-desert-research-station-hanksville.climate: The site is much warmer than Mars. Crew rotations run in the northern winter, and the field season ends in spring because of desert heat.
mars-desert-research-station-hanksville.hazards: Desert heat limits the field season.

mars-desert-research-station-hanksville.place: Mars Desert Research Station, near Hanksville, San Rafael Swell, Utah, USA
mars-desert-research-station-hanksville.summary: The Mars Desert Research Station is a habitat run by the Mars Society in the Utah desert, chosen for its Mars-like terrain and appearance. Crews live in the habitat and wear spacesuit simulators outside while they practice field tactics, habitat design and crew selection. Research there includes microbes in local rocks and desert soils.
mars-desert-research-station-hanksville.terrain_geology: The desert was chosen for its Mars-like terrain and appearance. The source we read does not describe the rock layers in detail.

mars-desert-research-station-lunar-crews.access_and_facilities: Hanksville is the nearest town, reached by road. Crews walk or use all-terrain vehicles for outings, and water is rationed.
mars-desert-research-station-lunar-crews.climate: Much warmer than Mars. The field season ends in northern spring because of desert heat.
mars-desert-research-station-lunar-crews.hazards: A fire once destroyed the original greenhouse, and part of the site is a foot-traffic-only zone.

mars-desert-research-station-lunar-crews.place: Mars Desert Research Station, near Hanksville, Utah, USA
mars-desert-research-station-lunar-crews.summary: The Mars Desert Research Station is a small habitat run by the Mars Society on the San Rafael Swell in southern Utah. Volunteer crews live and work there in simulated Mars missions, and a NASA-funded teacher training programme there simulates living on the Moon or Mars. The desert was chosen for its Mars-like terrain.
mars-desert-research-station-lunar-crews.terrain_geology: Desert terrain chosen for its Mars-like appearance. Rock-dwelling microbes called endoliths are often studied there.

mauna-kea-pisces-isru-test-sites.access_and_facilities: Saddle Road eased travel to the mountain, and summit access is restricted.
mauna-kea-pisces-isru-test-sites.climate: Alpine at the summit, with frost common all year and snow possible from the middle elevations up.

facts.label: RESOLVE field tests on Mauna Kea

mauna-kea-pisces-isru-test-sites.hazards: Altitude sickness is a risk at high elevation.

mauna-kea-pisces-isru-test-sites.place: Mauna Kea and PISCES test sites, Hawaii Island, Hawaii, USA
mauna-kea-pisces-isru-test-sites.summary: Mauna Kea is a dormant shield volcano on Hawaii Island whose volcanic cinder and tephra have been used as a stand-in for lunar soil. PISCES, a center at the University of Hawaii at Hilo, prepared a Mauna Kea test site for NASA field demonstrations of the RESOLVE in-situ resource experiment, which looked for hydrogen and water in the soil. The sources read disagree on the exact altitude of the test site, so the summit figures below describe the mountain, not the test pad.
mauna-kea-pisces-isru-test-sites.terrain_geology: The summit area has small cinder and pumice cones and lava domes built partly during past glaciations.

mcmurdo-dry-valleys-taylor-wright-valley.access_and_facilities: The valleys lie within the McMurdo Valleys Antarctic Specially Managed Area, so access is managed.
mcmurdo-dry-valleys-taylor-wright-valley.climate: Katabatic winds scour away snow and humidity, and evaporation and sublimation exceed precipitation. Above a certain elevation the air stays at or below freezing.

facts.label: Elevation above which air temperature stays at or below freezing

mcmurdo-dry-valleys-taylor-wright-valley.place: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Taylor and Wright valleys), Victoria Land, Antarctica
mcmurdo-dry-valleys-taylor-wright-valley.summary: The McMurdo Dry Valleys are the largest ice-free region of Antarctica and the coldest, driest desert in the world. Researchers treat them as the best known Earth analog of the Martian high northern plains where Phoenix landed, and as an astrobiology stand-in for Mars. The sources we read describe a Mars analog use; none of them describe a lunar cold-trap use.
mcmurdo-dry-valleys-taylor-wright-valley.terrain_geology: The valleys have granite and gneiss bedrock, glacial till and loose gravel. The upper permafrost is dry rather than ice-cemented, which resembles Martian soil.

merriam-crater-cinder-deposits.access_and_facilities: The source is a commercial quarry, and the simulant was made available to qualified investigators. The exact quarry position differs slightly between sources.

facts.label: Apollo sample matched by the JSC-1A simulant
