merriam-crater-cinder-deposits.place: Merriam Crater cinder deposits, San Francisco volcanic field, near Flagstaff, Arizona, USA
merriam-crater-cinder-deposits.summary: Merriam Crater is a cinder cone in the San Francisco volcanic field near Flagstaff, Arizona. NASA's JSC lunar mare soil simulants were mined from a commercial cinder quarry on the crater's flank. The later version was designed to match an Apollo mare soil sample.
merriam-crater-cinder-deposits.terrain_geology: The material is glass-rich basaltic ash that approximates the chemistry, mineral content, grain size and engineering behaviour of lunar mare soil. For the later version the ash was milled and sieved with no chemical processing.

meteor-crater-barringer.access_and_facilities: The crater is privately owned by the Barringer Crater Company. A visitor center sits on the north rim and guided rim tours run daily, weather permitting.
meteor-crater-barringer.climate: The dry Arizona climate and the crater's relatively young age are given as the reason it has changed little since it formed.

image.author: USGS National Map
image.credit: Aerial image: USGS National Map, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Meteor Crater - Arizona

meteor-crater-barringer.place: Meteor Crater (Barringer Crater), near Flagstaff and Winslow, Arizona, USA
meteor-crater-barringer.summary: Meteor Crater is an impact crater in the northern Arizona desert, between Flagstaff and Winslow. The Lunar and Planetary Institute and other science institutes call it the best-preserved meteorite crater on Earth. NASA astronauts trained in the crater before the Apollo missions to the Moon, and field training for astronauts continues there.
meteor-crater-barringer.terrain_geology: The crater has a squared-off outline thought to follow regional jointing in the rock layers. The centre is filled with rubble above the crater bedrock.

mistastin-kamestastin-lake-crater.access_and_facilities: The site is within the traditional hunting grounds of the Mushuau Innu First Nation, and visiting requires permission.

facts.label: First identified as a possible crater (year)

mistastin-kamestastin-lake-crater.place: Mistastin (Kamestastin) Lake crater, Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
mistastin-kamestastin-lake-crater.summary: Mistastin is a confirmed impact crater in northern Labrador, filled by a lake with an arc-shaped central island that is the crater's central uplift. It is used for field geology training of Canadian Space Agency and NASA astronauts. A doctoral thesis treats it as a lunar science and exploration analogue.
mistastin-kamestastin-lake-crater.terrain_geology: The target rock was a batholith of adamellite and mangerite with lenses of anorthosite. Shock features include shatter cones, melt rocks and glass.

moses-lake-sand-dunes.access_and_facilities: The dunes are southwest of the town of Moses Lake. The test team worked in an open treeless area with room for large equipment.

moses-lake-sand-dunes.place: Moses Lake sand dunes, Quincy Basin, Washington, USA
moses-lake-sand-dunes.summary: The Moses Lake dunes are a field of basaltic sand in the Quincy Basin of central Washington. NASA used the dunes in an earlier year to test prototype robots, rovers, cargo carriers, cranes and spacesuits for future lunar missions. NASA's JPL describes the field as the largest basaltic wind-blown sand accumulation on Earth.
moses-lake-sand-dunes.terrain_geology: Wind-blown sand made mostly of basalt fragments, with some quartz. Dunes on the east side are still active.

mount-erebus-dante-i-robot.access_and_facilities: The American McMurdo Station and the New Zealand Scott Base are on the same island.
mount-erebus-dante-i-robot.hazards: A sightseeing passenger aircraft crashed into the mountain, killing all aboard, and the ice caves can hold air with a high carbon dioxide share.

image.author: Richard Waitt, U.S. Geological Survey

mount-erebus-dante-i-robot.summary: Mount Erebus is an active volcano on Ross Island with a long-lived lava lake in its summit crater. Dante I, an eight-legged tethered walking robot, was taken to the crater rim there in a NASA and National Science Foundation project to develop technology for future Moon or Mars trips. The descent stopped when the fiber-optic cable was severed.
mount-erebus-dante-i-robot.terrain_geology: The volcano is a composite cone with a shield-like lower half, and its summit holds a persistent phonolite lava lake inside an inner crater.

mount-etna-summit-area-robex-arches.access_and_facilities: The volcano is near Catania, and the ARCHES operators worked from a control site in Catania, whose distance from the volcano is in the facts.
mount-etna-summit-area-robex-arches.hazards: Etna is one of the most active volcanoes in the world and is almost constantly active.

image.author: BenAveling
image.credit: Photo: BenAveling, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Mount Etna and Catania

mount-etna-summit-area-robex-arches.place: Mount Etna, Metropolitan City of Catania, Sicily, Italy
mount-etna-summit-area-robex-arches.summary: Mount Etna is an active stratovolcano whose lava fields and granular surface have been used to test robots for lunar missions. The Helmholtz ROBEX analog mission ran there first, and the German Aerospace Center later led the ARCHES demonstration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and ESA (dates are in the facts). In that demonstration an ESA astronaut drove the Interact rover remotely from Catania.
mount-etna-summit-area-robex-arches.terrain_geology: Etna is built of basaltic lava and ash above the boundary between the African and Eurasian plates.

mount-howe-and-the-scott-glacier-moraine.access_and_facilities: The Mount Howe area has the closest blue ice runway to the South Pole, where wheeled aircraft can land.
mount-howe-and-the-scott-glacier-moraine.climate: The area has no net annual snow accumulation. The source gives no temperature data.

facts.label: First seen by Byrd Antarctic Expedition

mount-howe-and-the-scott-glacier-moraine.place: Mount Howe, east side of Scott Glacier, Marie Byrd Land, Antarctica
mount-howe-and-the-scott-glacier-moraine.summary: Mount Howe is an elongated mountain near the head of Scott Glacier in Marie Byrd Land, apparently the southernmost mountain in the world. It is a rocky outcrop in the polar ice. In this project it is a candidate not in our reference list, and the sources checked here do not document planetary analog use.
mount-howe-and-the-scott-glacier-moraine.terrain_geology: It consists of low connecting ridges and gable-shaped rock peaks that stick up through the ice.

myvatn-and-krafla-lava-fields.access_and_facilities: Public land and nature reserve; paved roads; geothermal power plant area.
myvatn-and-krafla-lava-fields.climate: The climate is tundra bordering on subarctic, with cool summers and very long, cold winters.

facts.label: Apollo astronaut geology trips to Iceland

myvatn-and-krafla-lava-fields.hazards: Krafla is volcanically active and has erupted many times in recorded history.

image.author: Hansueli Krapf

myvatn-and-krafla-lava-fields.place: Mývatn and Krafla lava fields, northern Iceland
myvatn-and-krafla-lava-fields.summary: Mývatn is a shallow lake in an area of active volcanism in northern Iceland, next to the Krafla volcano. The ground around it is young basalt from fissure eruptions. Apollo astronaut groups did geology field training in Iceland, and the Exploration Museum lists Mývatn among the places the later group visited.
myvatn-and-krafla-lava-fields.terrain_geology: Mývatn formed in a large basaltic fissure eruption, and Dimmuborgir is a forest of rock pillars left where temporary lava lakes drained. Krafla is a caldera on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge with a long fissure zone.

myvatn-namafjall-hydrothermal-rootless-c.climate: Tundra climate with cool summers and long, cold winters.
myvatn-namafjall-hydrothermal-rootless-c.hazards: The area has active volcanism and earthquakes, and the Krafla activity in recent decades included land rise, rifting and eruptions.

image.author: Pjt56
image.credit: Photo: Pjt56, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Lake Myvatn

myvatn-namafjall-hydrothermal-rootless-c.summary: Myvatn is a shallow lake in a volcanically active part of northern Iceland, with rootless cones (pseudocraters) formed when lava met wet sediment and caused steam explosions. Nearby Namafjall has hot springs and fumaroles that alter basalt into clays and iron sulfates. Researchers have proposed Namafjall deposits as an analogue for sulfate soils at Gusev crater, and rootless cones have been compared with cones seen on Mars from orbit.
myvatn-namafjall-hydrothermal-rootless-c.terrain_geology: The lake formed after a large basaltic lava eruption. The shore has groups of pseudocraters and lava pillars, and Namafjall is a ridge of hyaloclastite.

namib-desert-gobabeb.access_and_facilities: The station is southeast of the port town of Walvis Bay, inside the national park.
namib-desert-gobabeb.climate: Hyperarid, with most of the little rain falling from December to May. Fog is common.

image.author: NASA GIBS
image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Namib Desert (Gobabeb), centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

namib-desert-gobabeb.summary: Gobabeb is a desert research station where the Kuiseb River, a large dune sea and gravel plains meet. It was founded by an Austrian entomologist and is now the Gobabeb Namib Research Institute. The page we read does not mention Mars; GSOP lists it as a reference for its large dune sea and permanent station.
namib-desert-gobabeb.terrain_geology: A dune sea lies south of the station and gravel plains lie north, with the dry Kuiseb riverbed between them.

navajo-sandstone-hematite-concretions-gr.access_and_facilities: The monument is reached by a scenic state highway and the Hole-in-the-Rock Road from Escalante, with visitor centers in Escalante and Kanab.

navajo-sandstone-hematite-concretions-gr.place: Navajo Sandstone iron concretions (Moqui marbles), Grand Staircase-Escalante region, Utah, USA
navajo-sandstone-hematite-concretions-gr.summary: Iron oxide concretions known as Moqui marbles weather out of the Jurassic Navajo Sandstone in southern Utah. A commentary in Nature noted that they look very like the hematite spherules, nicknamed blueberries, that the Opportunity rover found at Meridiani Planum. The same commentary says the Martian rocks differ in composition, and a later review says how the Utah concretions formed is still debated, which limits how far the comparison goes.
navajo-sandstone-hematite-concretions-gr.terrain_geology: The host rock is a dune-field sandstone, and the concretions are thought to have formed from groundwater that moved iron through the rock.

neemo-aquarius-reef-base.access_and_facilities: Crews live in the habitat for the whole mission because saturation diving needs a long decompression before surfacing. Florida International University has run it since it took over from the University of North Carolina Wilmington.

image.author: NASA
image.credit: Photo: NASA, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Aquarius habitat exterior

neemo-aquarius-reef-base.place: Aquarius Reef Base, off Key Largo, Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, Florida, United States
neemo-aquarius-reef-base.summary: Aquarius is an underwater research habitat that NASA uses for NEEMO, its long-running undersea spaceflight analog. NASA describes the focus as exploration science, spacewalk techniques and tools, and flight hardware and operations concepts. It is an analog for operations and isolation, not for terrain.
neemo-aquarius-reef-base.terrain_geology: The habitat sits on the seafloor next to a deep coral reef called Conch Reef.

newberry-volcano-big-obsidian-flow-lava-.access_and_facilities: A paved road reaches the caldera and a gravel section leads near Paulina Peak. The Lava Lands Visitor Center runs a seasonal shuttle.
newberry-volcano-big-obsidian-flow-lava-.climate: Precipitation falls as winter snow and summer rain, and the cave interior stays cold all year.

image.author: USGS photo by Lyn Topinka
image.credit: Photo: USGS photo by Lyn Topinka, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Newberry caldera with Paulina and East Lakes and Big Obsidian Flow

newberry-volcano-big-obsidian-flow-lava-.place: Newberry Volcano, Newberry National Volcanic Monument, near Bend, Oregon, USA
newberry-volcano-big-obsidian-flow-lava-.summary: Newberry is a large volcano south of Bend, Oregon, with a caldera, a young obsidian flow and a long lava tube called Lava River Cave. NASA trained Apollo astronauts there, including future lunar landing crews. The area is now a national volcanic monument open to visitors.
newberry-volcano-big-obsidian-flow-lava-.terrain_geology: The summit holds a caldera that formed in a major eruption. The Big Obsidian Flow is a young glassy lava flow, and Lava River Cave is the longest continuous lava tube in the state.

nordlinger-ries-crater.access_and_facilities: Nördlingen lies just south-west of the crater centre. The Ries Crater Museum in Nördlingen and the Ries Geopark are the main visitor resources.

nordlinger-ries-crater.place: Nördlinger Ries impact crater, Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, Germany
nordlinger-ries-crater.summary: The Ries is a large meteorite impact crater in southern Germany, with the town of Nördlingen close to its centre. Its ejecta deposits, including suevite and the Bunte Breccia, are well exposed. Wikipedia reports that an Apollo crew did geology field training there, and the Ries geopark says ESA astronauts have held field sessions there more recently.
nordlinger-ries-crater.terrain_geology: The suevite formed from shocked sedimentary rock, and the Bunte Breccia ejecta extends well beyond the crater rim. The impactor reached into the crystalline basement.

ojos-del-salado-high-altitude-permafrost.access_and_facilities: A Chilean national route passes north of the volcano. On the Chilean side a dirt road leads to mountain refuges, and most ascents use that side.
ojos-del-salado-high-altitude-permafrost.climate: Very cold, windy and dry. Precipitation is mostly hail and snow, and the dry air keeps glaciers to small patches of firn and ice in sheltered spots.

facts.label: Distance of the national route (Route 31) north of the volcano

ojos-del-salado-high-altitude-permafrost.hazards: The volcano ranks low for hazard, but summit ice means lahars are possible if it erupts.

ojos-del-salado-high-altitude-permafrost.place: Ojos del Salado, Chile and Argentina border, Atacama Region (Chile) and Catamarca Province (Argentina)
ojos-del-salado-high-altitude-permafrost.summary: Ojos del Salado is the highest volcano on Earth, on the Argentina and Chile border at the southern end of the Puna de Atacama. Researchers study its gullies, crater lakes and climate as possible Mars analogues. It is a candidate in our screening and is not in our reference list.
ojos-del-salado-high-altitude-permafrost.terrain_geology: The massif is made of overlapping lava domes, lava flows, cones and many craters, mostly potassium-rich dacite. Permafrost is expected from about the middle slopes upward, with buried ice under sand and moraines.

orocopia-mountains.access_and_facilities: The range lies south of the main interstate highway through the Colorado Desert.

image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Orocopia Mountains, centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

orocopia-mountains.place: Orocopia Mountains, Riverside County, California, USA
orocopia-mountains.summary: The Orocopia Mountains are a desert range east of the Coachella Valley in southern California. A Caltech geology professor used the range for geologic field training of Apollo crews. We found no source stating that anorthosite occurs here, so we cannot confirm the highland rock link in the reference list.
orocopia-mountains.terrain_geology: Known for Orocopia schist, a blueschist assemblage whose terrain was shaped mainly by movement on the San Andreas Fault.

painted-desert-petrified-forest.access_and_facilities: A main interstate highway crosses the park, and a park road links it to a second highway. Headquarters is east of Holbrook.
painted-desert-petrified-forest.climate: Cold semi-arid, with hot summers, freezing winters and most rain in August.
painted-desert-petrified-forest.hazards: Strong winds, sandstorms and dust devils are common, and prairie rattlesnakes live in the park.

image.author: Jeffhollett
image.credit: Photo: Jeffhollett, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Jasper Forest at Petrified Forest NP in AZ 12.jpg

painted-desert-petrified-forest.place: Painted Desert and Petrified Forest National Park, Arizona, USA
painted-desert-petrified-forest.summary: Petrified Forest National Park in northeastern Arizona includes part of the Painted Desert, a badland of banded, colorful clay-rich rock. The layers belong to the Late Triassic Chinle Formation. The page read does not discuss Mars; the Mars link on our list is a layered clay sequence in a dry setting that is easy to reach.
painted-desert-petrified-forest.terrain_geology: The Chinle Formation contains bentonite clay that swells when wet and cracks when dry, which keeps plants from growing on the slopes.

image.author: NASA GIBS
image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Pampas de La Joya, centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

pampas-de-la-joya.place: Pampas de La Joya, southern Peru
pampas-de-la-joya.summary: Pampas de La Joya is a hyper-arid patch of the Atacama Desert in southern Peru. Studies of its soils report high oxidant activity using methods similar to those on the Viking and Phoenix missions, and the identity of the oxidant is still unknown. Researchers compare it with the Yungay area in Chile, noting lower organic matter at La Joya.
pampas-de-la-joya.terrain_geology: The soils are hyper-arid desert soils, studied for their oxidants and organic content.

payun-matru-volcanic-field-and-pampas-on.access_and_facilities: Paved roads serve the area, with a national route to the west and another around the north and east. The volcano lies in the La Payunia provincial reserve.
payun-matru-volcanic-field-and-pampas-on.climate: The climate is cold and dry with strong westerly winds.
payun-matru-volcanic-field-and-pampas-on.hazards: The area has little water and is high and exposed.

image.author: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
image.credit: Photo: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.title: Payún volcanic field, Argentina (aerial)

payun-matru-volcanic-field-and-pampas-on.place: Payún Matrú volcanic field, Malargüe Department, Mendoza, Argentina
payun-matru-volcanic-field-and-pampas-on.summary: Payún Matrú is a large volcano and volcanic field in the Andean back-arc of Mendoza province, Argentina. Its Pampas Onduladas lava flow is described as the longest Quaternary lava flow in the world. In this project it is a candidate not in our reference list, and the sources checked here do not document planetary analog use.
payun-matru-volcanic-field-and-pampas-on.terrain_geology: The field's rocks range from alkali basalt to rhyolite, and basaltic volcanism has been active for a long time. Young flows are mostly rough aa lava, and the volcano has a large caldera.

peary-land-polar-desert-central-plateau.access_and_facilities: Two small research stations stand on Jørgen Brønlund Fjord, run by the Peary Land Foundation. In summer, travel between them is by boat, depending on ice conditions.
peary-land-polar-desert-central-plateau.climate: Precipitation is very low, and the area was not glaciated in the most recent ice age. Plants cover only a small part of the surface.
peary-land-polar-desert-central-plateau.hazards: Polar bears live in the area.

image.title: Peary Land, Greenland aerial photo

peary-land-polar-desert-central-plateau.summary: Peary Land is a peninsula in northeast Greenland that includes the most northerly ice-free land in the world. Most of its surface is polar desert, because the air is too dry to produce snow. Wikipedia does not describe it as a Moon or Mars analog; it is on our list as a candidate from our screening scores, not because an agency has used it that way.
peary-land-polar-desert-central-plateau.terrain_geology: The peninsula is cut by long fjords and rivers, with a heavily glaciated mountain range and an ice cap in the west. Zinc and lead deposits are known at Citronen Fjord.

pilbara-dresser-formation-stromatolites.place: Dresser Formation, North Pole Dome, Pilbara, Western Australia, Australia
pilbara-dresser-formation-stromatolites.summary: The Dresser Formation in the Pilbara Craton holds some of the oldest candidate traces of life on Earth, including stromatolites and other microbial structures in chert. Researchers argue that similar rocks could guide the search for life on Mars, and they cite its hot-spring deposits because Mars had silica-rich sinter at a similar time. Some researchers have challenged the biological origin of the structures.
pilbara-dresser-formation-stromatolites.terrain_geology: The formation forms a roughly circular ring of hills around the North Pole Monzogranite. The lowest chert unit holds barite and stromatolites, which are now mostly replaced by hematite.

pinacate-and-gran-desierto-el-pinacate.access_and_facilities: The reserve lies just south of the Arizona border; Puerto Penasco, Sonoyta and San Luis Rio Colorado are the nearest cities.

image.author: NASA GIBS
image.credit: Imagery: NASA GIBS, Landsat WELD annual composite, public domain. Ring marks the listed point.
image.title: Satellite view of Pinacate and Gran Desierto (El Pinacate), centred on the listed coordinates (Landsat WELD annual composite)

pinacate-and-gran-desierto-el-pinacate.place: El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve, Sonora, Mexico
pinacate-and-gran-desierto-el-pinacate.summary: El Pinacate is a volcanic field of cinder cones and large craters in the Sonoran Desert, surrounded by active dunes. NASA sent Apollo astronauts here to train for walking on the Moon because the terrain resembles the lunar surface. The area is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.
pinacate-and-gran-desierto-el-pinacate.terrain_geology: Volcanic shield with cinder cones and a high concentration of maar craters, ringed by extensive active dunes.

pisgah-volcanic-field-lavic-lake.access_and_facilities: The cone sits just south of an interstate highway and the old National Old Trails Highway, west of Ludlow. The crater and much of the lava field are private property, but nearby lava tubes are a popular caving destination.

pisgah-volcanic-field-lavic-lake.place: Pisgah Crater and Lavic Lake volcanic field, Mojave Desert, California, USA
pisgah-volcanic-field-lavic-lake.summary: Pisgah Crater is a cinder cone in the Mojave Desert and the youngest of four cones in the Lavic Lake volcanic field. Basalt flows run far from the cone across the desert floor. The page read does not describe any analog use; the Mars link on our list is a basalt flow beside a dry lake bed that can be used for calibration.
pisgah-volcanic-field-lavic-lake.terrain_geology: Flows extend far to the west and southeast of the cone. The summit was lowered by cinder mining.

pu-u-nene-cinder-cone-jsc-mars-1-source.access_and_facilities: The original supply ran out and a copy was later made by Orbitec; sources say that product was no longer available some years ago (year in the facts).

pu-u-nene-cinder-cone-jsc-mars-1-source.place: Pu'u Nene cinder cone, Island of Hawaii, Hawaii, United States
pu-u-nene-cinder-cone-jsc-mars-1-source.summary: The cinder cone is the source of the palagonitic tephra used to make the first widely used Mars soil simulant, made at NASA's Johnson Space Center. The weathered volcanic ash contains nanophase iron oxides that give it a spectrum similar to dusty Martian deposits. The simulant has known limits: it is mostly X-ray amorphous and differs from Mars in composition.
pu-u-nene-cinder-cone-jsc-mars-1-source.terrain_geology: The material is weathered volcanic ash made mostly of X-ray amorphous palagonite, a hydrated alteration product of volcanic glass.

qaidam-basin-dalangtan-playa.access_and_facilities: Railways cross the basin, including the Golmud to Dunhuang and Golmud to Korla lines.
qaidam-basin-dalangtan-playa.climate: The basin is hyperarid, with cool average temperatures, very high evaporation, large daily and seasonal swings and relatively high ultraviolet radiation.

qaidam-basin-dalangtan-playa.place: Qaidam Basin and Dalangtan playa, Haixi Prefecture, Qinghai province, China
qaidam-basin-dalangtan-playa.summary: The Qaidam Basin is a very dry basin on the north-eastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, with salt lakes, playas and yardangs. Dalangtan is one of its four main playas, in the north-west. The China Geological Survey has studied the basin as a Mars analog, to test spectroscopy methods and equipment for China's Mars rover programme.
qaidam-basin-dalangtan-playa.terrain_geology: The basin is a crescent-shaped intermontane basin ringed by the Kunlun, Qilian and Altyn-Tagh mountains, with very thick sediments. Saline lakes and playas cover about a quarter of it, and wind-carved yardangs occur in the desert.

rio-grande-gorge-taos.access_and_facilities: The Rio Grande Gorge Bridge crosses the gorge northwest of Taos.
rio-grande-gorge-taos.climate: The climate is semi-arid, with summer thunderstorms in July and August and possible snow from November through March.

rio-grande-gorge-taos.place: Rio Grande Gorge, near Taos, Taos County, New Mexico, USA
rio-grande-gorge-taos.summary: The Rio Grande Gorge is a deep canyon in northern New Mexico cut through basalt flows of the Taos Plateau volcanic field. Wikipedia reports that NASA gave Apollo astronauts geology training there, citing similarities to an Apollo landing site. That page does not call it a rille analog; the rille label comes from our own list.
rio-grande-gorge-taos.terrain_geology: The gorge lies within the Rio Grande Rift and cuts through stacked basalt flows. It was carved by erosion over several million years.

rio-tinto-marte.access_and_facilities: Copper mining was permitted to reopen after a long pause, so parts of the area are an active mining district.

rio-tinto-marte.place: Rio Tinto, Huelva province, Andalusia, Spain
rio-tinto-marte.summary: The Rio Tinto is a river in southwestern Spain with very acidic, iron-rich red water. Extremophile microbes live in it, and scientists have compared its water chemistry with the water in which the rocks at Meridiani Planum on Mars were deposited. Mining has gone on in the area for thousands of years, and it is unclear how much of the acidity is natural.
rio-tinto-marte.terrain_geology: The river flows through the Iberian Pyrite Belt, which has large sulphide ore deposits formed by hydrothermal activity on an ancient sea floor. Oxide terraces built by microorganisms are found well above the present water level.

salar-de-pajonales.climate: Arid and windy, with strong sunlight and low air pressure.
salar-de-pajonales.hazards: Dissolution pits and cavities in the crust can be as tall as a person.

salar-de-pajonales.place: Salar de Pajonales, Atacama Region, Chile
salar-de-pajonales.summary: Salar de Pajonales is a high-altitude salt flat in Llullaillaco National Park at the edge of the Atacama Desert. Low pressure, high salinity, aridity, large day and night temperature swings and strong ultraviolet light make it a model for Martian environments where life might persist. The climate here may have resembled that of Mars in its Hesperian period.
salar-de-pajonales.terrain_geology: A gypsum crust with domes, mounds, ridges and polygon cracks, surrounded by andesite and rhyolite rock with active hot springs.

salar-grande.access_and_facilities: It lies near the city of Iquique, on the eastern margin of the Coastal Range.
salar-grande.climate: Hyperarid, with morning fog from the sea called camanchaca.

salar-grande.summary: Salar Grande is a salt flat in northern Chile that sits near the coast, unlike most Chilean salars, which are high in the Andes. Researchers treat it as an analog for Martian chloride and perchlorate deposits because very dry conditions have lasted there for a long time. Fog from the sea is the main source of water for the halite, and halite nodules there host cyanobacteria.
salar-grande.terrain_geology: The basin holds mostly unaltered lake-bed chloride deposits in an extensional basin, with a thick body of banded and massive halite.

samail-ophiolite-wadi-tayin-massif.access_and_facilities: The Oman Drilling Project cored the crust-mantle transition and mantle peridotite in this massif.

samail-ophiolite-wadi-tayin-massif.place: Samail ophiolite, Wadi Tayin massif, Oman
samail-ophiolite-wadi-tayin-massif.summary: The Samail ophiolite is one of the largest and best-exposed pieces of oceanic crust and upper mantle on land. Researchers use it as an analog for Martian serpentinite environments, and one study mapped serpentine and carbonate there at fine scale as a test for orbital mineral detections. Mixed carbonate and serpentine are hard to tell apart at coarse scales, which is a caveat for the comparison.
samail-ophiolite-wadi-tayin-massif.terrain_geology: The Wadi Tayin massif has a thick mantle section of harzburgite with some dunite, overlain by gabbro, dikes and pillow lavas.

schirmacher-oasis-near-maitri-station.access_and_facilities: Maitri Station, installed in a late twentieth century programme, is a few kilometres from Novolazarevskaya and has meteorological, geomagnetic and seismological observatories. The source does not describe how the oasis is reached.
schirmacher-oasis-near-maitri-station.climate: The climate is mild for Antarctica, with a cold annual average and relatively frequent sunshine.

schirmacher-oasis-near-maitri-station.place: Schirmacher Oasis, Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica
schirmacher-oasis-near-maitri-station.summary: Schirmacher Oasis is an ice-free plateau on the Princess Astrid Coast of Queen Maud Land, between the ice sheet and an ice shelf. India's Maitri Station and Russia's Novolazarevskaya Station both stand on it. In this project it is a candidate not in our reference list, and the sources checked here do not document planetary analog use.
schirmacher-oasis-near-maitri-station.terrain_geology: The plateau is rocky ground that supports only mosses and lichens, with more than a hundred freshwater lakes. Rock outcrops rise from the ice sheet nearby.

sedan-crater-nevada-national-security-si.access_and_facilities: The nearest city is Mercury. The U.S. Department of Energy offers free monthly tours, and the crater is on the National Register of Historic Places.
sedan-crater-nevada-national-security-si.climate: Arid Mojave/Great Basin desert; hot summers, cold nights.

sedan-crater-nevada-national-security-si.place: Sedan Crater, Yucca Flat, Nevada National Security Site, Nevada, USA
sedan-crater-nevada-national-security-si.summary: Sedan Crater is a large crater made by an underground nuclear explosion test in the Plowshare programme, in Yucca Flat at the Nevada National Security Site. NASA used craters at the Nevada test site, including Sedan, to train Apollo astronauts, with Sedan serving as a stand-in for an impact crater. Because the yield and geometry of the explosion are documented, it is also used as a reference crater.
sedan-crater-nevada-national-security-si.terrain_geology: The explosive was placed in a shaft in deep desert alluvium, so the crater was dug into loose sediment, not hard rock.

shark-bay-hamelin-pool-stromatolites.access_and_facilities: The reserve is reached from the North West Coastal Highway by Hamelin Pool Road and the Telegraph Station grounds. A boardwalk is the only public access, and entry is free.

facts.label: Year the stromatolites were first reported by an oil survey

shark-bay-hamelin-pool-stromatolites.hazards: The environment is fragile, which is why public access is limited to a boardwalk.

shark-bay-hamelin-pool-stromatolites.place: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve, Shark Bay, Western Australia, Australia
shark-bay-hamelin-pool-stromatolites.summary: Hamelin Pool, in World Heritage-listed Shark Bay, has the most diverse and abundant living marine stromatolites in the world. Salt levels are about double those of normal seawater, which limits animals that would graze on the microbial mats. The sources we read do not make a Mars comparison, and our list marks the site as a living-stromatolite reference that fails our water test.
shark-bay-hamelin-pool-stromatolites.terrain_geology: Shallow, salty bay water with stromatolite columns built by cyanobacteria.

sittampundi-anorthosite-complex.access_and_facilities: Rock for the simulant came from the villages of Sithampoondi and Kunnamalai.

sittampundi-anorthosite-complex.place: Sittampundi anorthosite complex, near Salem, Tamil Nadu, India
sittampundi-anorthosite-complex.summary: The Sittampundi complex is an outcrop of anorthosite, a rock close in composition to lunar highland rock. ISRO made its highland lunar soil simulant in bulk from rock collected here. The simulant was used at ISRO's Lunar Terrain Test Facility in Bengaluru to test the lander and rover of the Chandrayaan mission.
sittampundi-anorthosite-complex.terrain_geology: Anorthosite rich in calcic plagioclase, with oxide proportions largely equivalent to lunar highland anorthosite according to the simulant paper.

sp-crater-and-sp-lava-flow.access_and_facilities: It lies north of Flagstaff, and the cone can be climbed.

sp-crater-and-sp-lava-flow.place: S P Crater and S P lava flow, San Francisco volcanic field, Arizona, USA
sp-crater-and-sp-lava-flow.summary: S P Crater is a basaltic andesite cinder cone north of Flagstaff in the San Francisco volcanic field, with a long lava flow running north from the vent. Wikipedia says American astronauts have used the crater to train for moonwalking. The cone can be climbed, and the flow can be viewed from the rim.
sp-crater-and-sp-lava-flow.terrain_geology: The cone has an agglomerate rim, and its lava flow comes from the same vent. Scientists debate whether the flow slightly predates the cone.

stillwater-complex.place: Stillwater igneous complex, Beartooth Mountains, southern Montana, United States
stillwater-complex.summary: The Stillwater complex is a large layered mafic intrusion. Its anorthosite and norite are the raw material for NASA's NU-LHT lunar highland regolith simulants, which are based on the average composition of Apollo highland soil samples. A newer simulant made by Washington Mills uses the same Stillwater rock approach.
stillwater-complex.terrain_geology: The complex is a layered mafic intrusion exposed along the north flank of the Beartooth Range. It has chromium ore and has been mined for palladium and other platinum group elements.

sudbury-basin.access_and_facilities: The city of Greater Sudbury sits on the basin's southern edge.

sudbury-basin.place: Sudbury Basin, Greater Sudbury, Ontario, Canada
sudbury-basin.summary: The Sudbury Basin is the eroded remnant of a very old impact crater in Ontario. NASA used it to train Apollo astronauts to recognise impact-formed rocks such as breccias. Trainees included the crews of three Apollo landing missions.
sudbury-basin.terrain_geology: Main rock units include footwall breccia, the Sublayer, the Sudbury Igneous Complex and the Whitewater Group. The basin's ores hold nickel, copper, gold, silver and platinum-group metals, mostly on the outer rim.

teide-las-canadas-caldera.access_and_facilities: A public road crosses the caldera, and a cable car runs from the roadside most of the way to the summit. A free permit is needed to climb the last section to the top.
teide-las-canadas-caldera.climate: Daily temperature swings are large, and precipitation is low, with part of it falling as snow.

teide-las-canadas-caldera.place: Las Cañadas caldera and Teide, Teide National Park, Tenerife, Spain
teide-las-canadas-caldera.summary: Las Cañadas is a large volcanic caldera on Tenerife with the Teide volcano rising from it. Wikipedia says Teide National Park is a useful volcanic reference point for studies related to Mars. Instrument teams have tested equipment there, including a Raman instrument tried out before its use on the ESA-NASA ExoMars mission.
teide-las-canadas-caldera.terrain_geology: The caldera is a horseshoe-shaped depression that opens to the north, with a high southern rim of cliffs. It is a volcanic terrain of lava and pumice.

tenoumer-crater.summary: Tenoumer is a small impact crater in the Sahara Desert of Mauritania, formed in Precambrian gneiss and granite. A volcanic origin was once proposed, but current evidence indicates an impact origin. It is a candidate in our screening and is not in our reference list, and the source we read does not describe it as an analog site.
tenoumer-crater.terrain_geology: Basalt and rhyodacite occur outside the crater basin. Sediments cover the crater bottom, and the rim stands well above the floor.

tirez-lake.climate: Alternating dry and wet periods over about two decades before total drying.

tirez-lake.summary: Tirez was a small, seasonal, very salty lagoon in central Spain that dried out completely. Researchers monitored its drying for about a quarter of a century and propose it as a time-resolved analog for the wet to dry transition on early Mars. The sources we read do not confirm the sulfate chemistry listed in the reference list.
tirez-lake.terrain_geology: A shallow closed-basin lagoon with very high salt content. A neighbouring lagoon in the same system is described as rich in salt and sulphur.

tottori-sand-dunes-lunar-demonstration-f.access_and_facilities: The dunes lie just outside Tottori city. The demonstration field has flat, slope and free-design zones.

tottori-sand-dunes-lunar-demonstration-f.place: Tottori Sand Dunes, Tottori Prefecture, Japan
tottori-sand-dunes-lunar-demonstration-f.summary: The Tottori Sand Dunes are a long coastal dune system on the Sea of Japan. A lunar demonstration field opened on the grounds of Tottori University's Arid Land Research Center, where companies and researchers can test lunar rovers and other equipment. A published study found the dune sand has mechanical properties closer to lunar regolith than the sand in many test facilities.
tottori-sand-dunes-lunar-demonstration-f.terrain_geology: Sediment from the Chugoku Mountains was carried by the Sendai River to the sea and shaped by wind into dunes, with bowl-shaped hollows and wind ripples.

umm-al-samim-sabkha.access_and_facilities: Wilfred Thesiger travelled through the area on his Oman journey.
umm-al-samim-sabkha.climate: The setting is a desert with little vegetation.

facts.label: Year Thesiger first crossed the area

umm-al-samim-sabkha.hazards: The crust can break and trap vehicles and people, like quicksand.

umm-al-samim-sabkha.place: Umm as Samim sabkha, eastern edge of the Rub al Khali, Oman
umm-al-samim-sabkha.summary: Umm as Samim is a very large salt flat at the foot of the Oman Mountains where groundwater collects. Its crust looks solid but can give way, and locals call it the Mother of Poisons. We found no Mars analog literature specific to this site; Mars analog work in the region has focused on the Samail ophiolite and the Abu Dhabi sabkha.
umm-al-samim-sabkha.terrain_geology: The flat is a salt marsh with a brackish crust and little vegetation, fed by drainage from the mountains and the wadis.

valley-of-ten-thousand-smokes-katmai.access_and_facilities: Visitors usually take a bus along the only road in the park, which starts at Brooks Camp.
valley-of-ten-thousand-smokes-katmai.hazards: The area has five active stratovolcanoes nearby, which the Alaska Volcano Observatory monitors.

valley-of-ten-thousand-smokes-katmai.place: Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes, Katmai National Park and Preserve, Alaska, USA
valley-of-ten-thousand-smokes-katmai.summary: The Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes is an ash-filled valley in Katmai National Park, formed by the Novarupta eruption in the early twentieth century, the largest eruption by volume of that century. NASA and the USGS trained Apollo astronauts there in two groups. Vegetation still does not grow on the valley floor.
valley-of-ten-thousand-smokes-katmai.terrain_geology: The valley is filled with ignimbrite and ash deposits. Early steam vents gave the valley its name, though few remain active.

vostok-station.access_and_facilities: The station was supplied from Mirny Station on the Antarctic coast.
vostok-station.climate: It is extremely cold all year, with very little precipitation that falls entirely as snow.

vostok-station.place: Vostok Station, Princess Elizabeth Land, East Antarctica
vostok-station.summary: Vostok is a Russian research station on the East Antarctic plateau, near the southern Pole of Cold. It holds the lowest air temperature ever recorded on Earth. Wikipedia does not describe it as a Moon or Mars analog; on our list it is a cold reference point, based on its temperature record.
vostok-station.terrain_geology: The station sits on thick ice, and Lake Vostok lies far below the surface.

white-sands-gypsum-dunes.access_and_facilities: The park lies on the north side of a main highway, southwest of Alamogordo, and is surrounded by White Sands Missile Range.
white-sands-gypsum-dunes.climate: Cold semi-arid climate, with hot summer afternoons and cold winter nights.
white-sands-gypsum-dunes.hazards: The park and the highway close during missile tests, and errant missiles have fallen inside the park.

white-sands-gypsum-dunes.place: White Sands National Park, Tularosa Basin, New Mexico, USA
white-sands-gypsum-dunes.summary: White Sands protects part of the largest gypsum dunefield on Earth. Gypsum dunes on Mars are known from Olympia Undae near the north pole, and researchers have used White Sands to study how gypsum sand moves and sorts. A recent conference abstract proposes White Sands measurements as ground truth for the Martian dunes.
white-sands-gypsum-dunes.terrain_geology: Gypsum from ancient seas was dissolved by rain and carried into the basin, where wind breaks the crystals into sand. Lake Lucero is a dry lakebed in the southwest, and the Alkali Flat is a remnant of an ice age lake.

wolfe-creek-crater.access_and_facilities: The crater lies in a national park south of Halls Creek and is reached by the Tanami Road.

wolfe-creek-crater.place: Wolfe Creek crater, Great Sandy Desert, Western Australia, Australia
wolfe-creek-crater.summary: Wolfe Creek is a large, well-preserved meteorite crater in the Great Sandy Desert of northern Western Australia. It is known as Kandimalal to the Djaru people. Wikipedia calls it arguably the second most obvious meteorite crater on Earth after Barringer Crater; the page does not describe it as a lunar analog.
wolfe-creek-crater.terrain_geology: An exposed, undrilled impact structure with iron meteorite fragments and iron oxide shale balls around it.

yellowstone-norris-geyser-basin.access_and_facilities: Boardwalks and marked trails serve the basin from the park's main loop road.

yellowstone-norris-geyser-basin.hazards: Several people have died after falling into hot springs, so visitors must stay on boardwalks and marked trails.

yellowstone-norris-geyser-basin.place: Norris Geyser Basin, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, USA
yellowstone-norris-geyser-basin.summary: Norris Geyser Basin is described in an NPS-derived listing as the hottest, oldest and most dynamic thermal area in Yellowstone. Unlike most basins in the park, its water is acidic. Mars researchers compare silica deposits near Home Plate in Gusev crater with hydrothermal settings on Earth, but the sources read do not tie Norris to Mars in particular, and one study argued that El Tatio in Chile is a closer match than Yellowstone.
yellowstone-norris-geyser-basin.terrain_geology: The basin lies near the northwest edge of the Yellowstone caldera and builds silica sinter around vents. It includes Steamboat Geyser, the tallest active geyser in the world.
